- Role: Finance Manager (Remote)
- Location: Remote (Work from Anywhere)
- Job Type: Full-Time
- Payout: $400K - $550K/yr


Role Overview:
We are hiring for one of our clients in the finance sector, seeking a Strategic Project Lead, Finance Expertise to drive high-impact financial initiatives. This role requires deep financial acumen to align projects with strategic business objectives and deliver measurable outcomes.


Key Responsibilities:
• Lead cross-functional finance projects with a focus on cost optimization and revenue growth.
• Develop and implement financial strategies to support long-term business planning.
• Partner with executive leadership to assess financial risks and opportunities.
• Oversee budgeting, forecasting, and financial modeling for project execution.
• Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and internal financial policies.


Required Skills & Qualifications:
• Experience managing financial projects in a corporate or consulting environment.
• Strong proficiency in financial analysis, modeling, and strategic planning.
• Ability to translate complex financial data into actionable business insights.
• Expertise in financial software, ERP systems, and data visualization tools.
• Track record of delivering projects on time and within budget.


More About the Opportunity:
This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a global leader in the financial services industry, contributing to the modernization of financial operations. The position plays a critical role in shaping the company’s financial future through data-driven decision-making.


Equal Opportunity Employer:
We hire based on skills and expertise. All qualified candidates are welcome regardless of background, experience, or prior employment history. Applications are reviewed solely on demonstrated technical ability and qualifications.


Apply Now!

opportunity.job_description:
Client Accounting Manager
Remote | UK-Based | Gaming Industry


A fast-growing gaming business is looking to appoint a Client Accounting Manager to play a key role in supporting a portfolio of innovative studios and founders across the UK. This is a unique opportunity to join a specialist finance team that partners with gaming businesses throughout their growth journey, providing a blend of accounting, reporting, commercial finance and strategic support. The role offers significant autonomy, exposure to founder-led businesses, and the chance to help shape and build a growing finance function.


The Opportunity
As Client Accounting Manager, you will act as a trusted finance partner to multiple gaming and entertainment businesses, helping them strengthen financial processes, improve reporting, manage compliance obligations and make informed commercial decisions.
This is an excellent role for a qualified accountant who enjoys a blend of hands-on accounting, business partnering and process improvement within high-growth entrepreneurial environments.


Key Responsibilities

- Manage a portfolio of gaming and digital entertainment clients as their primary finance contact
- Build strong relationships with founders and leadership teams, supporting day-to-day financial operations
- Produce monthly management accounts, including P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reporting
- Deliver meaningful KPI reporting, financial insights and performance analysis
- Support budgeting, forecasting and cash flow planning
- Implement and improve finance systems, controls and processes
- Ensure compliance with statutory reporting and regulatory requirements
- Assist with financial modelling and business planning activities
- Contribute to the development of scalable internal processes and best practice frameworks
- Work closely with colleagues to deliver a high-quality, joined-up finance service


About You

- Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent)
- Strong financial accounting and management reporting experience
- A background in business services client accounting would be highly advantageous
- Experience supporting multiple stakeholders in fast-paced environments
- Proven ability to improve processes, systems and controls
- Strong commercial awareness and analytical capability
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills
- Self-motivated, proactive and comfortable working autonomously
- Previous experience with cloud-based finance systems such as Xero is advantageous


What's on Offer?

- Fully remote role with flexibility to be based anywhere in the UK
- Opportunity to work with innovative businesses within the gaming sector
- Broad role combining accounting, reporting, commercial finance and advisory work
- High levels of autonomy and visibility with business founders and leadership teams
- Professional development and long-term progression opportunities
- Collaborative, entrepreneurial and low-politics culture
- Private medical insurance, life assurance and generous holiday allowance

Coral Springs, FL (Remote) MUST LIVE IN SOUTH FLORIDA

Salary: $95,000 – $105,000 + Bonus

About The Company

Join a well-established, high-growth organization with over 40 years of industry success and a strong expansion strategy into new markets. The company is recognized for its innovative services, advanced technology, and continued investment in infrastructure.

The culture is collaborative, inclusive, and growth-oriented, with a strong emphasis on integrity, continuous improvement, and professional development. Employees benefit from excellent leadership, stability, and long-term career opportunities.

Why This Opportunity Stands Out



- 100% remote flexibility with a stable, growth-focused organization
- Strong leadership and a collaborative team environment
- Opportunity to contribute to a company actively expanding into new markets
- Career advancement and professional development opportunities
- Competitive compensation plus bonus and comprehensive benefits

Key Responsibilities



- Prepare and post journal entries across income statement, balance sheet, and intercompany accounts
- Perform general ledger reconciliations and account analyses with a high degree of accuracy
- Support month-end and year-end close processes
- Conduct variance analysis and ensure compliance with GAAP
- Maintain audit-ready financials and assist with external audits
- Partner with internal teams and vendors to resolve discrepancies
- Identify and implement process improvements and strengthen internal controls
- Prepare ad hoc financial reports and analysis for leadership
- Support special projects and ongoing accounting initiatives

Qualifications



- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Business Administration (MBA a plus)
- Minimum 5+ years of progressive accounting experience
- Strong knowledge of GAAP and financial reporting
- CPA preferred
- Experience with ERP systems (Great Plains a plus)
- Advanced Excel skills
- Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment while working remotely

opportunity.job_description:
Join the Rapidly Growing Team at Attivo Partners!


Are you dedicated to excellence and eager to advance your career? Passionate about technology and startups? Excited to work with some of the most innovative early-stage companies in the world? If so, Attivo Partners is the place for you!


Why Attivo?


Attivo Partners is a fast-growing full-service finance and accounting consulting firm headquartered in San Francisco, with a presence in major startup hubs across the US. Our remote teams specialize in providing fractional CFO and accounting services to venture-backed emerging growth clients, supporting their journey from inception to over $50M in revenue.


What We Offer:



- Collaborative Environment: Work alongside a talented team with extensive experience in venture-backed companies. At Attivo, we believe in teamwork and value the unique insights and creativity each member brings.
- Culture of Growth: We thrive on the challenges presented by diverse and exciting clients, offering unparalleled learning and professional development opportunities.
- Mentorship and Training: We are committed to nurturing talent and providing ongoing mentoring and training to help you grow personally and professionally.
- Flexibility: We understand the importance of balance and are dedicated to maintaining a culture that supports your career and personal life.


Our Values:



- Lasting Relationships: We build solid and enduring connections with our clients and team members.
- Data-Driven Insights: We leverage data to drive intelligent decisions and impactful results.
- Growth-Focused Mindset: We embrace opportunities for continuous improvement and innovation.
- Collaboration-First: We prioritize teamwork and believe the best solutions come from working together.
- Culture-Conscious: We foster a supportive and inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.


Join us at Attivo Partners and be part of a team that's shaping the future of finance and accounting for startups. Let's grow together!


Role Overview


The ideal Senior Accountant candidate is a resourceful problem solver who will take ownership of critical accounting tasks and will be a key player in ensuring the accounting and reporting function will scale and support the company’s rapid growth. Enthusiasm and willingness to learn are key to the success of the Senior Accountant.


This is a work from home position with location preference in the San Francisco/Bay Area, Los Angeles/Southern California, New York City, Austin, and Boston. Some travel to in-person company events is required, approximately 2-3 weeks out of the year. In-person onboarding training will take place within the first 3 months of employment (locations vary).


Responsibilities



- Perform day to day accounting duties in AP, AR, cash management, payroll, FA, GL and other duties as assigned

opportunity.job_description:
Salary: $100,000 to $115,000 + superannuation
Location: Australia
Work style: Full-time | Fully remote role


To be considered, you must currently reside in Australia and be an Australian citizen or permanent resident.


Why This Role
This is an opportunity for an experienced Senior Accountant to join a growing boutique accounting and advisory firm operating on a fully remote basis.


The role will suit someone who is technically strong, proactive, and confident in managing work without close supervision. You will be trusted to take ownership, communicate clearly and deliver high-quality work across tax, compliance and business services matters.


This is not a traditional suburban accounting role where the Partner reviews every detail before anything moves forward. The firm is looking for someone who can operate with care, judgement and accountability, while still having access to support when needed.


The role offers strong flexibility, broader client exposure and the opportunity to work in a firm that values responsiveness, commercial thinking and practical advice.


About Our Client
Our client is a boutique accounting and advisory firm supporting business owners, medical professionals, property investors and private clients.


The firm provides tax compliance, business advisory, structuring, cash flow support, SMSF and property-related advice.


The leadership team brings experience across Big 4 tax, international tax, mergers and acquisitions, strategy consulting and private client advisory. That background flows through to the firm's approach, which is focused on high-quality advice, responsiveness and helping clients make better commercial decisions.


The firm operates fully remotely, with regular team communication, daily check-ins, shared workflow lists, and modern systems that support collaboration across the team.


The Role
As a Senior Accountant, you will work across tax, accounting and business services matters for a diverse client base.


Your responsibilities will include:

- Preparing income tax returns for individuals, sole traders, companies, trusts and SMSFs
- Preparing financial statements and detailed working papers
- Preparing BAS and state tax returns, including payroll tax and land tax where required
- Preparing work through to review stage
- Researching tax issues and assisting with advice for senior team members and clients
- Liaising with the ATO, clients and other professionals
- Supporting tax planning and broader advisory work where appropriate
- Working with business owners, medical professionals, property investors and private clients
- Using Xero, Excel and other accounting systems to deliver accurate, timely work
- Contributing to process improvement as the firm continues to grow


This role is best suited to someone who wants to be hands-on, trusted and accountable, rather than someone who needs close supervision or prefers a heavily managed environment.


What You'll Bring

- At least 2+ years of experience in an Australian accounting firm
- Strong Senior Accountant-level capability across tax and business services
- Accounting degree from an Australian institution
- CA or CPA completed or underway
- Strong technical knowledge of Australian accounting and taxation fundamentals
- Experience preparing financial statements and tax returns for multiple entity types
- Strong Excel skills
- Experience with Xero
- Experience with MYOB AE, Logit or Karbon will be useful but is not essential
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Ability to manage deadlines and workflow in a fully remote environment
- High attention to detail and strong professional judgement
- A proactive approach to solving problems before they escalate
- Australian citizenship or permanent residency


What's On Offer

- $100,000 to $115,000 + superannuation
- Fully remote role within Australia
- Career progression opportunities
- Paid professional association fees
- Regular professional development
- Direct access to experienced firm leadership
- Exposure to business owners, medical professionals and property investors
- Opportunity to build stronger advisory capability over time
- Modern remote working model with regular team communication
- Supportive boutique team environment
- A firm culture built around trust, autonomy, responsiveness and quality work


Next Steps
To apply, please submit your resume and academic transcript.
Applications without both documents may not be considered.


For a confidential discussion, contact Shaun at Minchin Recruitment:
hello@minchinrecruitment.com.au
(07) 3733 3544


#SCR-shaun-minchin

opportunity.job_description:
Tax & Business Advisory Accountant
 
Looking for a firm that's invested in your future? We've Got Your Back.
Great accountants don't just prepare tax returns—they change lives.
At EnVision Partners, we believe accounting is about far more than numbers.
It's about helping business owners make better decisions, reduce stress, grow their wealth and create a legacy for future generations.


That's why our promise to every client—and every member of our team—is simple: We've Got Your Back.
As our business continues to grow, we're looking for an Accountant or Senior Accountant who wants more than a job. We're looking for someone who wants to build trusted relationships, challenge themselves professionally and be part of a team that's shaping the future of regional business.
Whether you're based in Chinchilla or anywhere across Queensland, we'd love to hear from you.


Why Join EnVision Partners?
We know you have options. So why choose EnVision? Because here, you're more than another employee.
You'll join a team that genuinely supports one another, values new ideas and believes your career should be just as important as the success of our clients.


What you'll enjoy:
✔ An attractive salary package based on your experience
✔ Flexible working arrangements, including remote work opportunities throughout Queensland
✔ A supportive and friendly team culture where We've Got Your Back isn't just a slogan—it's how we work every day
✔ The opportunity to work directly alongside experienced leaders and influence the future direction of the firm
✔ Ongoing mentoring, professional development and genuine career progression
✔ Exposure to business advisory, strategic planning and value-added client work—not just compliance
✔ A diverse client portfolio across retail, commercial, primary production, investment and professional services
✔ A workplace that embraces innovation, cloud technology and AI to help us deliver even better outcomes
✔ Modern systems that allow you to spend more time advising clients and less time on administration


What You'll Be Doing
You'll become a trusted adviser to a portfolio of clients, helping them navigate every stage of their business journey.


Your work will include:

- Preparing financial statements and tax returns
- Preparing BAS and IAS
- Tax planning and compliance advice
- Assisting with business structures and strategic planning
- Budgeting, forecasting and cash flow management
- Working closely with business owners to identify opportunities for growth
- Building long-term client relationships
- Working with Xero and cloud-based accounting systems
- Liaising with the Australian Taxation Office


You'll Thrive Here If You...
We're not looking for someone who's simply good with numbers.
We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys helping people.
You'll fit right in if you:

- Enjoy building lasting client relationships.
- Like solving problems and thinking beyond compliance.
- Want to be part of a supportive, high-performing team.
- Take pride in producing quality work.
- Embrace technology and continuous improvement.
- Are curious, motivated and always looking to learn.
- Believe that great client service starts with genuinely caring.


About You
You'll ideally have:

- A Bachelor of Accounting or related qualification
- CPA or CA qualification (or working towards it)
- Experience within public practice accounting
- Strong knowledge of Australian taxation legislation

Fully Remote Transaction Advisory Services Manager OR Senior Manager
Top 10 CPA Firm
Full-Time • $125,000–$195,000 base + Bonus (At least 20%)
Consistently pay out 100%+ of target bonus


About the Practice
This Top 10 CPA Firm's Transaction Advisory Services (TAS) group is a leading national due diligence practice supporting middle‑market private equity groups and companies. The team specializes in helping clients make informed investment decisions through high‑impact financial and operational analysis.


The practice has experienced significant growth, more than doubling in size over the past two years (currently sits at 40 employees) and is looking to hire a fully remote Transaction Advisory Services Manager OR Senior Manager.


What truly differentiates this team is its people‑first culture, entrepreneurial mindset, and commitment to real work‑life balance.


Why candidates are excited about this role:

- Fully remote with minimal travel
- Market‑leading compensation + strong bonus potential
- Manager: $125,000 - $155,000 Base + 20% Bonus (twenty percent is the floor)
- Senior Manager: $155,000 - $195,000 Base + 25% Bonus (twenty-five percent is the floor)
- Predictable schedules and genuine respect for personal time
- 40 to 45-hour work week
- Direct client exposure and long‑term relationship building
- Leadership support, growth opportunities, and merit‑based promotions


About the Role
The Transaction Advisory Services Manager OR Senior Manager will support private equity groups and companies through both buy‑side and sell‑side financial due diligence engagements. You will analyze target company financials, identify risks and opportunities, and provide insights that influence valuation, deal structure, and strategic decisions.


Preferred Qualifications

- CPA (or CPA‑eligible); strong understanding of U.S. GAAP.
- Master’s in Accounting or MBA with accounting undergrad preferred.
- 2–4+ years of financial audit experience (ideally with a top‑ten public accounting firm).
- 1–3 years in a TAS practice at a national accounting firm, including at least 1 year at the Manager level.
- Excellent communication skills — written and verbal.
- Advanced Excel skills; strong MS Office proficiency.
- Self‑driven, entrepreneurial, and able to thrive in a fast‑paced environment.


About the Organization
The broader organization is a nationally recognized professional services platform supporting middle‑market businesses across accounting, tax, advisory, benefits, insurance, and technology. With 10,000+ team members across 160+ U.S. locations, the company provides forward‑thinking insights and impactful client solutions.

opportunity.job_description:
At Common Trust, we're on a mission to make employee ownership the norm, not the exception. We help business owners sell their businesses to their employees, creating shared prosperity that strengthens companies, communities, and the broader economy. Common Trust has worked with businesses that have enabled over 63,000 workers to become employee-owners to date with a 93% client satisfaction rating, but for us, this is just the beginning.


With 75% of all business owners in the US looking to sell over the next decade, we believe that making employee ownership the transition of choice for small businesses is one of the most powerful ways for business owners to transition competitively, close the wealth gap in America, and build an economy worthy of passing on to the next generation. In this role, you'll be at the center of working with the business owners making it happen.


Learn more about us: Common-Trust.com




Position Summary


In response to growing demand, our advisory team is now hiring a Transaction Advisory Manager to guide small and mid-sized business owners through the sale of their businesses to their employees.


Reporting to the Chief Client Services Officer, you'll partner closely with clients to help them understand the financial, tax, estate, governance, and long-term business implications of an employee ownership transition. You'll prepare financial analyses, facilitate client discussions, and build trusted relationships that support a smooth and successful ownership transition.


This is a remote position that can be based anywhere in the United States. We work across multiple U.S. time zones and gather in person several times each year for team meetings and occasional industry events.


While we are seeking a highly motivated, intellectually curious individual who has strong foundational knowledge in business, legal, and financial matters, we are pleased to provide structured on-boarding and training to build fluency in employee ownership structures and Common Trust’s advisory approach.




Key Responsibilities



- Guide business owners through the process to sell their business to their employees, including analyzing the opportunities and risks associated with the sale, evaluating the sale proceeds, estate impact, tax outcomes, decision-making and governance, long-term company stability, and employee benefits alongside the client’s corporate counsel where relevant.
- Develop and maintain financial models to evaluate transaction structures, operating forecasts, financing alternatives, cash flow generation, debt repayment capacity, and scenario analyses that support client decision-making and long-term ownership transition planning.
- Translate complex information regarding financial, legal, estate, and tax matters in terms that clients can understand so they can make values-aligned decisions.
- Collaborate with and project manage trust, estate, and corporate attorneys to ensure clients receive the best legal advice and their goals are integrated into the legal documentation for the transaction.
- Collaborate with clients’ accounting and tax professionals to ensure clients receive thorough and actionable guidance with respect to the employee ownership sale and post-sale tax outcomes.
- Facilitate employee engagement meetings to help employees understand the impact of the employee ownership sale.
- Prepare clear, decision-oriented client deliverables, including financial models, scenario analyses, and recommendations that synthesize goals, risks, tradeoffs, and key transaction and governance terms.
- Build long-term, trusted client relationships.
- Contribute to our company culture of continuous learning by ensuring that learnings about our clients are captured and shared across the organization, and with company support, pursuing your own individual learning and development in your role. We view learning, feedback and growth as shared responsibilities.




Education and Experience



- Education in business, finance, entrepreneurship, public policy, sustainability, or a related program is a plus, however we place equal value on relevant work experience that demonstrates the skills and character traits needed to be successful in this role
- 3+ years of experience in a client-facing advisory role navigating complex business, legal, and/or financial decisions; such as in any of the following: corporate finance, corporate development, valuation, wealth management, financial services, management consulting, or paralegal with a particular focus on corporate governance, mergers and acquisitions for small and mid-sized businesses, and/or trust and estate law
- Experience developing multi-year operating forecasts, cash flow projections, financing models, or transaction analyses for privately held businesses is a plus
- First-hand experience (either personal or professional) that provides a knowledgeable and compassionate understanding of the decisions a business owner will face when they are ready to transition out of owning their company is a plus
- Experience building scalable systems and processes in an early-stage, entrepreneurial environment is a plus




Skills and Character Traits



- Strong attention to detail when dealing with complex legal and tax information and comfort with distilling the implications of such information for a range of audiences
- Advanced financial modeling skills, including the ability to build and modify integrated operating, cash flow, financing, and scenario models to evaluate transaction structures and long-term business performance
- Strong understanding of corporate finance principles, including cash flow forecasting, debt financing, capital structure, valuation, and financial statement analysis
- Advanced Excel skills, including experience building dynamic financial models
- Ability to translate complex financial analyses into practical recommendations for business owners and other non-financial stakeholders
- Ability to build authentic and trusted relationships with small business owners, senior leaders, and workers of various backgrounds across the U.S.
- Excellent organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders, timelines, and workstreams simultaneously
- Strong verbal and written communication skills, including comfort communicating complex legal, corporate governance, and financial topics to an audience that may not be familiar with technical financial or legal language
- Adaptability and willingness to work on a small team and take on the range of tasks necessary to deliver a high-quality product to clients, solve hard problems, and take initiative in improving processes
- Comfort working in a fast-paced, remote environment
- Proactive communication style, including the ability to manage up and keep internal and external stakeholders aligned on progress, risks, and next steps
- Interest in learning how to integrate new technologies into our workflows, including AI
- Passion for our mission to build a more prosperous and competitive economy through shared ownership




Why Join Our Mission


Our clients are inspiring and successful small business owners. Our clients are industry agnostic, located anywhere in the US, and range from $300,000 to $5M+ in EBITDA. Most business owners launched their company 20+ years ago, have a strong track record of profitability, and want to reward their long-term employees who helped build the successful business.


You will join a small, elite team with opportunity to make a real impact. Common Trust has approximately 10-15 employees, and the advisory team currently includes three incredibly talented, dynamic individuals who are shaping the way we do business. Two members of the advisory team have been with the company since its founding, and every member of the team has driven key innovations that are helping us scale our work while maintaining exceptional customer satisfaction. We are seeking another dynamo who wants to help us learn and improve the way we work, with plenty of opportunity for innovation and sharing ideas!


The work is hard and interesting. The Employee Ownership Trust structure was first utilized for business ownership in 2014, and is growing in popularity. Common Trust has been a key player in pioneering the structure, supporting businesses worth over $813M in aggregate to transition to EOT ownership. The work to uncover the efficiencies with respect to transaction structure, tax, and estate impacts that will help take this model to scale is not done!




What We Offer



- Opportunity to shape the future of business ownership in the U.S.
- A values-driven culture that prioritizes integrity, inclusion, and long-term thinking
- Compensation: $100,000 - $130,000 base salary, commensurate with experience; and an equity incentive plan


Benefits:

- Remote and flexible work schedule and environment
- Monthly coworking stipend + one-time home office stipend
- Health insurance: 99% medical and 50% vision/dental covered by employer
- 401(k) retirement plan
- Unlimited paid time off
- Paid parental leave plan




Equal Opportunity Employer


Common Trust provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, creed, national origin, sex, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, familial status, military status, height and weight, genetic predisposition or carrier status, arrest record, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. We strongly encourage people of color, people with disabilities, women, and LGBTQ candidates to apply.

evaluation.job_description:
At Common Trust, we're on a mission to make employee ownership the norm, not the exception. We help business owners sell their businesses to their employees, creating shared prosperity that strengthens companies, communities, and the broader economy. Common Trust has worked with businesses that have enabled over 63,000 workers to become employee-owners to date with a 93% client satisfaction rating, but for us, this is just the beginning.


With 75% of all business owners in the US looking to sell over the next decade, we believe that making employee ownership the transition of choice for small businesses is one of the most powerful ways for business owners to transition competitively, close the wealth gap in America, and build an economy worthy of passing on to the next generation. In this role, you'll be at the center of working with the business owners making it happen.


Learn more about us: Common-Trust.com




Position Summary


In response to growing demand, our advisory team is now hiring a Transaction Advisory Manager to guide small and mid-sized business owners through the sale of their businesses to their employees.


Reporting to the Chief Client Services Officer, you'll partner closely with clients to help them understand the financial, tax, estate, governance, and long-term business implications of an employee ownership transition. You'll prepare financial analyses, facilitate client discussions, and build trusted relationships that support a smooth and successful ownership transition.


This is a remote position that can be based anywhere in the United States. We work across multiple U.S. time zones and gather in person several times each year for team meetings and occasional industry events.


While we are seeking a highly motivated, intellectually curious individual who has strong foundational knowledge in business, legal, and financial matters, we are pleased to provide structured on-boarding and training to build fluency in employee ownership structures and Common Trust’s advisory approach.




Key Responsibilities



- Guide business owners through the process to sell their business to their employees, including analyzing the opportunities and risks associated with the sale, evaluating the sale proceeds, estate impact, tax outcomes, decision-making and governance, long-term company stability, and employee benefits alongside the client’s corporate counsel where relevant.
- Develop and maintain financial models to evaluate transaction structures, operating forecasts, financing alternatives, cash flow generation, debt repayment capacity, and scenario analyses that support client decision-making and long-term ownership transition planning.
- Translate complex information regarding financial, legal, estate, and tax matters in terms that clients can understand so they can make values-aligned decisions.
- Collaborate with and project manage trust, estate, and corporate attorneys to ensure clients receive the best legal advice and their goals are integrated into the legal documentation for the transaction.
- Collaborate with clients’ accounting and tax professionals to ensure clients receive thorough and actionable guidance with respect to the employee ownership sale and post-sale tax outcomes.
- Facilitate employee engagement meetings to help employees understand the impact of the employee ownership sale.
- Prepare clear, decision-oriented client deliverables, including financial models, scenario analyses, and recommendations that synthesize goals, risks, tradeoffs, and key transaction and governance terms.
- Build long-term, trusted client relationships.
- Contribute to our company culture of continuous learning by ensuring that learnings about our clients are captured and shared across the organization, and with company support, pursuing your own individual learning and development in your role. We view learning, feedback and growth as shared responsibilities.




Education and Experience



- Education in business, finance, entrepreneurship, public policy, sustainability, or a related program is a plus, however we place equal value on relevant work experience that demonstrates the skills and character traits needed to be successful in this role
- 3+ years of experience in a client-facing advisory role navigating complex business, legal, and/or financial decisions; such as in any of the following: corporate finance, corporate development, valuation, wealth management, financial services, management consulting, or paralegal with a particular focus on corporate governance, mergers and acquisitions for small and mid-sized businesses, and/or trust and estate law
- Experience developing multi-year operating forecasts, cash flow projections, financing models, or transaction analyses for privately held businesses is a plus
- First-hand experience (either personal or professional) that provides a knowledgeable and compassionate understanding of the decisions a business owner will face when they are ready to transition out of owning their company is a plus
- Experience building scalable systems and processes in an early-stage, entrepreneurial environment is a plus




Skills and Character Traits



- Strong attention to detail when dealing with complex legal and tax information and comfort with distilling the implications of such information for a range of audiences
- Advanced financial modeling skills, including the ability to build and modify integrated operating, cash flow, financing, and scenario models to evaluate transaction structures and long-term business performance
- Strong understanding of corporate finance principles, including cash flow forecasting, debt financing, capital structure, valuation, and financial statement analysis
- Advanced Excel skills, including experience building dynamic financial models
- Ability to translate complex financial analyses into practical recommendations for business owners and other non-financial stakeholders
- Ability to build authentic and trusted relationships with small business owners, senior leaders, and workers of various backgrounds across the U.S.
- Excellent organizational and project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders, timelines, and workstreams simultaneously
- Strong verbal and written communication skills, including comfort communicating complex legal, corporate governance, and financial topics to an audience that may not be familiar with technical financial or legal language
- Adaptability and willingness to work on a small team and take on the range of tasks necessary to deliver a high-quality product to clients, solve hard problems, and take initiative in improving processes
- Comfort working in a fast-paced, remote environment
- Proactive communication style, including the ability to manage up and keep internal and external stakeholders aligned on progress, risks, and next steps
- Interest in learning how to integrate new technologies into our workflows, including AI
- Passion for our mission to build a more prosperous and competitive economy through shared ownership




Why Join Our Mission


Our clients are inspiring and successful small business owners. Our clients are industry agnostic, located anywhere in the US, and range from $300,000 to $5M+ in EBITDA. Most business owners launched their company 20+ years ago, have a strong track record of profitability, and want to reward their long-term employees who helped build the successful business.


You will join a small, elite team with opportunity to make a real impact. Common Trust has approximately 10-15 employees, and the advisory team currently includes three incredibly talented, dynamic individuals who are shaping the way we do business. Two members of the advisory team have been with the company since its founding, and every member of the team has driven key innovations that are helping us scale our work while maintaining exceptional customer satisfaction. We are seeking another dynamo who wants to help us learn and improve the way we work, with plenty of opportunity for innovation and sharing ideas!


The work is hard and interesting. The Employee Ownership Trust structure was first utilized for business ownership in 2014, and is growing in popularity. Common Trust has been a key player in pioneering the structure, supporting businesses worth over $813M in aggregate to transition to EOT ownership. The work to uncover the efficiencies with respect to transaction structure, tax, and estate impacts that will help take this model to scale is not done!




What We Offer



- Opportunity to shape the future of business ownership in the U.S.
- A values-driven culture that prioritizes integrity, inclusion, and long-term thinking
- Compensation: $100,000 - $130,000 base salary, commensurate with experience; and an equity incentive plan


Benefits:

- Remote and flexible work schedule and environment
- Monthly coworking stipend + one-time home office stipend
- Health insurance: 99% medical and 50% vision/dental covered by employer
- 401(k) retirement plan
- Unlimited paid time off
- Paid parental leave plan




Equal Opportunity Employer


Common Trust provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, creed, national origin, sex, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, familial status, military status, height and weight, genetic predisposition or carrier status, arrest record, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. We strongly encourage people of color, people with disabilities, women, and LGBTQ candidates to apply.

About The Team

The Corporate Development team at DoorDash is a small, fast-paced, high-performing group responsible for sourcing, evaluating, negotiating and executing M&A and investments. This team is central to DoorDash’s continued growth. We work closely with senior leadership, operations, product and finance teams to guide company strategy. We lead all aspects of identifying, evaluating, and executing transactions that have a significant impact on the overall direction of the company.

About The Role

As a manager, you will identify and execute transformative acquisitions and investments globally that accelerate or increase the likelihood of DoorDash achieving its strategic objectives. You will report to the Director, Corporate Development. This role is remote first with some domestic and international travel expected.

You’re Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will…



- Participate in all aspects of the deal cycle, including sourcing, evaluation of business model attractiveness, strategic/financial analysis, valuation, due diligence, structuring and negotiation, and integration
- Build relationships with leaders at emerging and established companies as well as with investment banking, venture capital, and private equity firms
- Coordinate diligence, deal execution, and integration across cross-functional teams, including operations, engineering, product, finance, accounting, and legal
- Identify, research and recommend industries, companies and technologies for DoorDash to evaluate from an M&A or investment perspective and analyze the company's objectives and identify, recommend and pursue technologies that can accelerate those goals
- Develop and maintain financial models, dashboards and presentations that track and analyze our industry, as well as track prospective M&A opportunities
- Support cross-functional capital markets and financing efforts

Title: Integration Manager – M&A

Remote: Candidates in Eastern Time Zones

Supporting: IOA - Home Office (M&A Integration)

Requirements: Bachelors Degree in Business (or related field), 8-10 years P&C insurance experience managing a book

Please note: If this position is posted as either fully remote and/or hybrid, in accordance with company policy, individuals residing within a 50-mile radius of a branch location may be required to work onsite in a hybrid capacity as there may be occasions when on-site presence is necessary to meet specific business needs. Additionally, our remote work policy includes having a dedicated, distraction-free workspace. Remote work is not a substitute for childcare, elder care, or other personal responsibilities during working hours. To view our branch locations, please visit: ioausa.com/locations

About the Role: The Integration Manager is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing merger and acquisition integration projects and large-scale transformation initiatives across the organization. This role serves as a key liaison between executive leadership, cross-functional teams, acquired entities, and external partners to ensure successful integration outcomes. The Integration Manager develops project frameworks, manages risks, tracks milestones, and drives organizational alignment to ensure initiatives remain on schedule, within budget, and aligned with strategic business objectives.

Key Responsibilities



- Integration Strategy & Planning: Define project objectives, integration roadmaps, timelines, success measures, and governance structures that support organizational goals. 
- Project Scope & Requirements: Collaborate with stakeholders to define project scope, establish objectives, identify dependencies, and ensure alignment with business priorities. 
- M&A Integration Leadership: Lead merger and acquisition integration initiatives, coordinating cross-functional workstreams to support successful business transitions. 
- Transformation Program Management: Oversee large-scale transformation projects, ensuring alignment of processes, systems, teams, and operational objectives. 
- Resource Coordination: Manage internal resources, third-party vendors, and project stakeholders to ensure appropriate allocation of support and capabilities. 
- Project Execution & Monitoring: Develop and maintain detailed project plans, monitor progress, and ensure milestones are achieved within established timelines and budgets. 
- Change Management: Manage project changes, scope adjustments, and implementation activities while maintaining stakeholder alignment and project integrity. 
- Risk Management: Identify project risks, develop mitigation strategies, and proactively address issues that may affect integration or transformation success. 
- Stakeholder Communication: Develop communication plans and provide regular updates to leadership regarding project status, risks, decisions, and outcomes. 
- Performance Measurement: Utilize project management tools, metrics, and reporting frameworks to evaluate progress and measure initiative success. 
- Documentation & Governance: Maintain comprehensive project documentation, integration plans, decision logs, and governance records throughout the project lifecycle. 
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with business leaders, operational teams, technology teams, Finance, HR, and external stakeholders to drive alignment and execution. 
- Process Improvement: Evaluate business processes, identify opportunities for operational enhancement, and implement scalable solutions that improve effectiveness and efficiency. 
- Leadership & Professional Development: Demonstrate effective project leadership while continuously strengthening project management and organizational change capabilities. 
- Champion IOA Values: Demonstrate integrity, leadership, accountability, and professionalism in all interactions. 

Ideal Candidate Qualifications



- Bachelor’s degree in Business or a related field required; MBA preferred 
- 8-10+ years of project management and P&C insurance experience 
- Experience leading M&A integrations, organizational transformations, or large-scale enterprise initiatives preferred 
- PMP certification preferred 
- Strong project management, organizational, and stakeholder management skills 
- Exceptional analytical, conceptual thinking, and problem-solving abilities 
- Proven ability to influence stakeholders and drive alignment across multiple teams 
- Experience creating executive-level reports, presentations, and project documentation 
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook 
- Demonstrated success leading complex projects from planning through execution and delivery 
- Strong communication, prioritization, and time management skills 
- Proven leadership capability with a track record of driving results and managing competing priorities 

What We Offer



- Competitive salaries and bonus potential 
- Company-paid health insurance 
- Paid holidays, vacations, and sick time 
- 401K with employer match 
- Professional growth and career progression opportunities 
- Respectful culture and work/family life balance 
- Community service commitment 
- Supportive teammates and a rewarding work environment 

What To Expect (Application Process)



- 30-Minute Phone Screen, Online Assessments, and Interview(s). 

Salary Range

The expected pay range for this position is $100,000.00- $130,000.00 per year, depending on experience, relevant skills, and geographic location.

Insurance Office of America is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Top National Firm – Transaction Advisory Services Practice
Remote – U.S. Based


Manager - $125,000 - $155,000 w/ 20% Bonus (twenty percent is the floor, some high performing individuals see bonus up to and past 100%)


A top national professional services firm is continuing to expand its Transaction Advisory Services (TAS) practice, supporting middle‑market private equity groups and corporate buyers across the U.S. The TAS team specializes in financial due diligence for both buy‑side and sell‑side M&A transactions and has experienced significant, sustained growth over the last several years.


This group is known for its supportive leadership, collaborative culture, strong work‑life balance, and market‑leading compensation model. Team members work fully remote, enjoy minimal travel requirements, and have significant exposure to clients and leadership regardless of tenure. Promotions are merit‑based, not time‑based, creating real pathways for accelerated career progression.


If you are looking to join an entrepreneurial, high‑growth M&A due diligence team where your work has impact and your development is prioritized, this is an excellent opportunity.


What You’ll Do

- Lead and manage financial due diligence engagements for private equity and corporate clients.
- Serve as the primary point of contact with clients throughout the transaction process.
- Review and analyze financial statements, working capital trends, profitability drivers, cash flows, and potential risks or liabilities.
- Provide insights and recommendations related to key deal considerations, valuation implications, and business trends.
- Prepare detailed reports and present findings to clients.
- Oversee engagement teams, provide guidance, and ensure high‑quality deliverables.


Preferred Qualifications

- Master’s degree in Accounting or MBA with an accounting background preferred.
- 2–4+ years of financial audit experience (Big 10 firm preferred), investment banking, FDD, corporate finance, or similar M&A experience.
- 1–3+ years of Transaction Advisory Services experience at a national accounting or advisory firm, including at least 1 year at the Manager level.
- Strong technical accounting knowledge (U.S. GAAP).
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Advanced Excel skills; strong proficiency in MS Office.
- Highly self‑motivated, entrepreneurial, and able to thrive in a fast‑paced environment.


Minimum Requirements

- Bachelor’s degree required.
- CPA License
- 6+ years of relevant experience.
- 3+ years of supervisory experience.
- Financial Due Diligence (FDD), Quality of Earnings (Q of E)
- Ability to manage all aspects of client engagements.
- Strong communication ability across all levels of an organization.
- Proficiency in relevant technology platforms.
- Ability to travel if needed (minimal).

Job Title: Financial Accountant
Company: Leading Healthcare Group (Confidential)
Location: 100% remote-based role! (CFO based in Melbourne so preference would based in VIC)
Remuneration: $80,000 – $85,000 + Super

About the Role

Supporting 500 clinicians across 6 healthcare brands, our client is a rapidly expanding healthcare group seeking a hands-on Financial Accountant. Acting as a key partner to the CFO, you will manage a service-based cost model focused on revenue, margin, and onshore/offshore salary structures. This position offers direct Board exposure, full ownership of month-end reporting and budgeting, and a dedicated technical oversight role across offshore operations.

Key Responsibilities

Month-End Close & Financial Reporting


- Own the month-end close calendar across all group entities, maintaining accuracy while working to optimize and reduce close timelines.
- Prepare monthly management accounts for individual entities and the consolidated group, including manual journals.
- Provide clear variance commentary against budget and forecast, explaining movements in commercial terms rather than purely accounting language.
- Review the monthly balance sheet reconciliation pack, implementing clear ageing and resolution plans for reconciling items.
- Prepare board and leadership reporting packs in conjunction with management, and support external audit processes.Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Analysis


- Coordinate and build annual budgets across all entities, establishing key assumptions with operational leaders.
- Maintain rolling financial and cash flow forecasts, highlighting timing risks and working capital pressures early.
- Contribute financial modelling and commercial analysis for pricing decisions, new service lines, and structural changes.Offshore Output Review & Quality Assurance


- Perform technical reviews on work delivered by 2 offshore finance team members, covering AP/AR, bank recs, clinician pay runs, onshore payroll support, and GL coding.
- Verify transactions are coded consistently against group accounting policies and the chart of accounts across all entities.
- Review bank, clearing, and control account reconciliations to ensure reconciling items are genuine and resolved promptly.
- Provide constructive, documented feedback and build process notes, checklists, and templates to lift output quality over time.
- Note: The offshore team is managed directly by the CFO. This role acts as a technical review function and does not carry line management responsibilities.Group Policy, Compliance & Controls


- Ensure correct and consistent accounting treatment compliant with Australian Accounting Standards (AASB) and internal policy.
- Maintain and update the group chart of accounts and procedure documentation as the business expands.Selection Criteria

Essential


- Education & Qualification: CA or CPA qualified (or currently completing studies), with a relevant degree in Accounting, Commerce, or Finance.
- Technical Experience: Strong core experience in financial accounting, month-end close, consolidated group reporting, and budgeting/forecasting.
- Systems & Excel: Advanced Excel skills (handling large data sets and building multi-entity financial models) and proficiency in Xero.
- Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication, with an ability to translate complex financial results for non-finance stakeholders and clinicians.
- Mindset: Highly autonomous with a "roll up your sleeves" approach to balance detailed transactional review with high-level reporting.Desirable


- Prior experience in healthcare, allied health, clinical services, or NDIS environments.
- Experience working alongside or reviewing output from offshore/outsourced finance teams.
- Exposure to multi-entity groups undergoing rapid growth or restructuring.

Supporting 500 clinicians across 6 healthcare brands, our client is a rapidly expanding healthcare group seeking a hands-on Financial Accountant. Acting as a key partner to the CFO, you will manage a service-based cost model focused on revenue, margin, and onshore/offshore salary structures. This position offers direct Board exposure, full ownership of month-end reporting and budgeting, and a dedicated technical oversight role across offshore operations.

Key Responsibilities

Month-End Close & Financial Reporting


- Own the month-end close calendar across all group entities, maintaining accuracy while working to optimize and reduce close timelines.
- Prepare monthly management accounts for individual entities and the consolidated group, including manual journals.
- Provide clear variance commentary against budget and forecast, explaining movements in commercial terms rather than purely accounting language.
- Review the monthly balance sheet reconciliation pack, implementing clear ageing and resolution plans for reconciling items.
- Prepare board and leadership reporting packs in conjunction with management, and support external audit processes.Budgeting, Forecasting & Financial Analysis


- Coordinate and build annual budgets across all entities, establishing key assumptions with operational leaders.
- Maintain rolling financial and cash flow forecasts, highlighting timing risks and working capital pressures early.
- Contribute financial modelling and commercial analysis for pricing decisions, new service lines, and structural changes.Offshore Output Review & Quality Assurance


- Perform technical reviews on work delivered by 2 offshore finance team members, covering AP/AR, bank recs, clinician pay runs, onshore payroll support, and GL coding.
- Verify transactions are coded consistently against group accounting policies and the chart of accounts across all entities.
- Review bank, clearing, and control account reconciliations to ensure reconciling items are genuine and resolved promptly.
- Provide constructive, documented feedback and build process notes, checklists, and templates to lift output quality over time.
- Note: The offshore team is managed directly by the CFO. This role acts as a technical review function and does not carry line management responsibilities.Group Policy, Compliance & Controls


- Ensure correct and consistent accounting treatment compliant with Australian Accounting Standards (AASB) and internal policy.
- Maintain and update the group chart of accounts and procedure documentation as the business expands.Selection Criteria

Essential


- Education & Qualification: CA or CPA qualified (or currently completing studies), with a relevant degree in Accounting, Commerce, or Finance.
- Technical Experience: Strong core experience in financial accounting, month-end close, consolidated group reporting, and budgeting/forecasting.
- Systems & Excel: Advanced Excel skills (handling large data sets and building multi-entity financial models) and proficiency in Xero.
- Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication, with an ability to translate complex financial results for non-finance stakeholders and clinicians.
- Mindset: Highly autonomous with a "roll up your sleeves" approach to balance detailed transactional review with high-level reporting.Desirable


- Prior experience in healthcare, allied health, clinical services, or NDIS environments.
- Experience working alongside or reviewing output from offshore/outsourced finance teams.
- Exposure to multi-entity groups undergoing rapid growth or restructuring.

opportunity.job_title: Senior Manager, Financial Intelligence Unit, MEA
opportunity.job_description:
Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at circle.com.

What You’ll Be Part Of

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. We have built a flexible work environment where new ideas are encouraged and everyone is a stakeholder.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

As a Manager within Circle’s Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), you will safeguard Circle’s integrity by leading financial crime investigations and intelligence efforts across the UAE and broader MEA region. You will identify, analyze, and report suspicious activity while ensuring compliance with AML and sanctions regulations. This role requires close collaboration with global FIU and compliance teams, product stakeholders, and regional regulators. You will enhance detection capabilities, respond to evolving typologies, and ensure that Circle meets the highest standards of integrity and compliance excellence in the region.

What You'll Work On



- Design and implement MEA-specific compliance frameworks, including developing alignments with both local regulatory requirements (CBUAE, VARA) and global standards.
- Lead comprehensive financial crime risk assessments to identify regional vulnerabilities, ensuring Circle’s risk appetite and controls are optimized for MEA’s evolving landscape.
- Act cross-functionally within Financial Crime Compliance, providing expert support across broader compliance domains including Sanctions, KYC, and Transaction Monitoring. 
- Oversee and perform complex investigations into potential financial crimes and suspicious activities, leveraging deep local major markets knowledge to interpret regional transaction patterns and behaviors.

opportunity.job_title: Group Finance Project Manager - Forensic Accounting
opportunity.job_description:
Group Finance Project Manager – Forensic Accounting
£130,000–£145,000 | 12 Month FTC | London | 4–5 days office based


I’m working with a leading global investment management business looking to hire an experienced Group Finance Project Manager on a 12-month fixed-term contract.


Reporting directly to the Global Head of Group Finance, this is a senior, hands-on forensic accounting and finance project role, focused on investigating and resolving historical accounting issues, improving the quality of group reporting and strengthening financial controls across a complex international business.


The successful candidate will take ownership of a range of projects including:

- Forensic review and resolution of historical accounting entries and balances
- Reviewing historical consolidation journals and determining appropriate accounting treatment
- Retained earnings and balance sheet reconciliation projects
- Strengthening balance sheet controls and reconciliation processes
- Reviewing and improving reporting across co-investment structures
- Supporting improvements to UK and global finance processes
- Assisting with consolidated financial statements and statutory reporting
- Implementing stronger financial accounting and reporting controls across the global platform
- Strong use of Hyperion / HFM


We’re looking for a fully qualified accountant (ACA/ACCA/CIMA or equivalent) with significant post-qualified experience and a strong background in forensic accounting, technical accounting and financial control.


You’ll need strong IFRS and UK GAAP knowledge, consolidation experience (Hyperion/HFM), excellent balance sheet and financial control expertise, and the ability to investigate complex historical accounting issues and drive them through to resolution.


You’ll also need strong executive presence and the confidence to engage credibly with Board-level stakeholders, auditors and other senior parties, alongside the ability to work autonomously and deliver against demanding deadlines.


This would particularly suit someone with a background in Forensic Accounting, Group Finance, Financial Control or Technical Accounting who enjoys project-based work and can come into a complex environment, identify historical issues and get them resolved.


£130,000–£145,000 per annum
12-month FTC
London – ideally 4–5 days per week in the office

The opportunity

In Assurance at EY, we empower you to thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment. As a key player in our assurance practice, you'll engage with diverse clients, providing critical insights that drive their success. We offer a wealth of career opportunities, from hands-on experience with cutting-edge technologies to tailored professional development programs. Our culture fosters collaboration, innovation, and a commitment to excellence, ensuring that every team member feels valued and inspired to reach their full potential. Discover your future with us and be part of a team that makes a difference!

Financial Crime & Forensics is part of EY’s Financial Services practice: we work closely with financial services clients and regulators to help prevent, investigate and remediate fraud and financial crime along with other regulatory risks and issues.

Our Financial Services clients are increasingly requesting our support with reacting to developments in the crypto assets landscape. Our dedicated Investigations & Compliance team supports them in the aftermath of fraud or financial crime events, to proactively prepare for future events and with regulatory issues. Join us and you will work on challenging projects in a rapidly growing team, accelerating your career within an international and supportive environment. You'll also be introduced to career challenges that will take you into exciting new professional territory.

The role

As a Financial Crime & Forensics Crypto Manager, you will supervise and develop junior colleagues, briefing them and reviewing their work, whilst executing your own work to a standard requiring minimal review across a portfolio of clients and internal projects. You will be expected to take personal responsibility for leading engagements and ensuring that deadlines are met to our clients’ satisfaction.

Your role will also include proactively establishing, maintaining and strengthening internal and external relationships. Your knowledge and experience will help to create commercial insights for our clients.

Within the Financial Crime & Forensics team you will work on the execution of a variety of projects including investigations, financial crime framework reviews, risk assessments, claims and disputes, fraud and financial crime prevention, and compliance programme development within the financial services sector.

Required Skills And Experience



- Knowledge and professional experience of crypto assets
- Experience of working in the financial services sector
- Strong academic record including a degree (in any subject)
- Experience of managing juniors, including coaching of discrete tasks and reviewing outputs
- Proficiency in Excel, Word and PowerPoint
- Assertive and confident interpersonal skills
- Ability to simultaneously handle diverse and pressing assignments and sensitive and adversarial situations
- Ability to think critically with very good attention to detail 
- Being comfortable working both independently and in a team

Ideally you will also have



-  Professional accountancy or other financial qualification such as ICA, CFE or CAMS

What We Look For

We’re interested in leaders with a genuine creative vision and the confidence to make it happen. If you are serious about forensics and enthusiastic about solving our clients’ most complex issues, this role is for you.

What We Offer You

At EY, we’ll develop you with future-focused skills and equip you with world-class experiences. We’ll empower you in a flexible environment, and fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive culture of globally connected teams. Learn more.

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

To help create the best experience during the recruitment process, please describe any disability-related adjustments or accommodations you may need.

opportunity.job_description:
About Revolut

People deserve more from their money. More visibility, more control, and more freedom. Since 2015, Revolut has been on a mission to deliver just that. Our powerhouse of products — including spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more — help our 80+ million customers get more from their money every day.

As we continue our lightning-fast growth,‌ 2 things are essential to our success: our people and our culture. In recognition of our outstanding employee experience, we've been certified as a Great Place to Work™. So far, we have 13,000+ people working around the world, from our offices and remotely, to help us achieve our mission. And we're looking for more brilliant people. People who love building great products, redefining success, and turning the complexity of a chaotic world into the simplicity of a beautiful solution.

About The Role

Our Audit team is critical to our business. They work closely with Risk and Compliance to create internal risk management and compliance processes, and make sure they’re running efficiently.

We're looking for an Internal Auditor to oversee the development and execution of internal audits focused on FinCrime topics, including financial crime risk management, KYC, ongoing due diligence, transaction monitoring, and sanctions screening.

Up to shape what's next in finance? Let's get in touch.

What You'll Be Doing



- Partnering with Head of FinCrime Audit to design audit programmes under internal audit policies, regulatory requirements, and the Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing
- Looking for ways to make the best use of data as part of our audit process, including to inform our understanding of risks, test controls, and provide relevant insights to the business
- Providing input and assisting in the identification of relevant risks and regulatory requirements for incorporation as part of our audit scope
- Interacting with staff to obtain an understanding of relevant risks, controls, and processes
- Communicating and discussing findings with management
- Developing audit reports that identify deficiencies and underlying root causes, providing recommendations to mitigate/address deficiencies while adding value to Revolut
- Following up on reviews of deficiencies noted during audits
- Conducting research and completing assigned training requirements necessary to maintain relevance
- Monitoring audit progress (against expected timelines, scope, etc.) and managing projects to completion, escalating promptly where required
- Supporting UK audits across financial services, operational risk, and technology

What You'll Need



- 5+ years of experience in an audit-related role within a regulated financial services environment
- An undergraduate or master's degree in a quantitative discipline
- A solid understanding of the current regulatory environment, including EU Money Laundering Directives, FCA requirements, UK Money Laundering Regulations, and JMLSG Guidance
- Proficiency in working with and interpreting data
- A desire to learn, grow, and have impact quickly as part of an expanding team
- Critical thinking and problem-solving skills
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
- Proficiency with relevant technology and tools
- Solid organisational and project management skills
- Impeccable attention to detail

Nice to have



- Experience in a fast-paced environment with a focus on execution
- Proficiency in SQL, SAS, Python, RACA, or CIA

Building a global financial super app isn’t enough. Our Revoluters are a priority, and that’s why in 2021 we launched our inaugural D&I Framework, designed to help us thrive and grow everyday. We're not just doing this because it's the right thing to do. We’re doing it because we know that seeking out diverse talent and creating an inclusive workplace is the way to create exceptional, innovative products and services for our customers. That’s why we encourage applications from people with diverse backgrounds and experiences to join this multicultural, hard-working team.

Important notice for candidates:

Job scams are on the rise. Please keep these guidelines in mind when applying for any open roles.



-  Only apply through official Revolut channels. We don’t use any third-party services or platforms for our recruitment.
-  Always double-check the emails you receive. Make sure all communications are being done through official Revolut emails, with an @revolut.com domain.

We won't ask for payment or personal financial information during the hiring process. If anyone does ask you for this, it’s a scam. Report it immediately.

By submitting this application, I confirm that all the information given by me in this application for employment and any additional documents attached hereto are true to the best of my knowledge and that I have not wilfully suppressed any material fact. I confirm I have disclosed if applicable any previous employment with Revolut. I accept that if any of the information given by me in this application is in any way false or incorrect, my application may be rejected, any offer of employment may be withdrawn or my employment with Revolut may be terminated summarily or I may be dismissed. By submitting this application, I agree that my personal data will be processed in accordance with Revolut's Candidate Privacy Notice

opportunity.job_description:
Job Description



- Part of the CFAS division
- Involved in the assessment of business interruption and other financial losses arising on behalf of clients.
- Negotiating and settlement of claims.
- Work within and part of the wider GTS team.
- Travel and undertake site visits and external meetings
- Marketing and promotion of self and business both internally and externally

Responsibilities



- Work both externally and internally assessing business interruption and financial claims
- Receiving and reviewing and analysing financial information.
- Preparing reports commenting in detail on the review and conclusion of analytical work.
- Visiting Insurers, Reinsurers, Claimants and the Insured.
- Communicating regularly with all interested parties, calculating and approving interim payments, preparing interim reports and other communication.
- Calculating and agreeing settlement of claims, and preparing final reports.
- Assisting in the development of less experienced staff members.
- Additionally developing working relationships with existing clients and helping to identify and plan approaches to new clients.
- Maintain and update files and records keeping fully up to date on any technical or legal changes which may have a bearing on a case.
- Identifying and developing business opportunities for self and team.

Qualifications



- Problem solving ability in order to recognise difficulties and take the appropriate steps to address the issues
- Quality focussed to provide a high level of customer service both internally and externally
- Ability to demonstrate high attention to detail
- Dispute and resolution handling skills in order to manage cases effectively and proactively
- Competent use of technology
- Ability to work on own initiative and within a team environment
- Behave in a strongly customer focused way at all times to ensure development and maintenance of client relationships
- Demonstrate personal integrity in a way which is consistent to the company’s core values
- Communicate effectively by sharing, listening and exchanging information and knowledge at all levels
- Build and maintain positive working relationships
- Demonstrate a solution and action oriented style in order to deliver against targets
- Demonstrate a flexible and resilient operational style
- Demonstrated behaviours must be in close alignment with Crawford stated values: RESTORE

Essential



- Experienced in Forensic Accounting and/or Business Interruption claims.
- Accountancy qualification.
- Experience of managing staff

Desirable



- Strong communication skills (written and verbal)
- Good customer service, organisational & communication skills

About Us

Crawford & Company is the world's largest publicly listed independent provider of claims management and outsourcing solutions. For over 85 years, we've combined global expertise, industry-leading technology, and a people-first approach to help restore and enhance lives, businesses, and communities.

With more than 9,000 colleagues across 70+ countries, we're united by a shared purpose and commitment to delivering exceptional outcomes for our clients. We call this One Crawford.

In addition to compelling career opportunities that span countless fields and disciplines, Crawford & Company also offers employees a competitive salary with a strong benefits package and ongoing training and mentorship programs through every stage of your career. To find out more about working at Crawford & Company, take a look here.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

About

At Crawford & Company we are committed to creating an inclusive work environment. We don’t just talk about diversity and inclusion; we aim to infuse it into everything we do – underpinning our strategy with three core elements:

Consciousness 

Capability

Culture

 We are also proud to be a Disability Confident Committed Employer. We are committed to accommodating applicants with disabilities throughout the hiring process.

If you have an accommodation need, please email recruitment@crawco.co.uk as soon as possible to make any reasonable adjustments.

So, what are you waiting for? Apply today, we’re looking forward to your application.
