opportunity.job_description:
About Net At Work

Founded in 1996, Net at Work is one of North America’s largest technology advisors and solution providers for small and mid-size businesses. Our award-winning consultancy offers a rich portfolio of next-generation technology, industry expertise, implementation and managed services to help organizations derive value from the transformative benefits of technology.

Through the integration of ERP, HCM and/or CRM solutions, Net at Work offers unique, industry-specific solutions and operation platforms that enable companies to compete more effectively in today’s digital economy. For more information, visit www.netatwork.com.

About This Position

The Manager, M&A Integration is responsible for leading the operational integration of acquired businesses from transaction close through full operational stabilization. This role serves as the central integration leader responsible for coordinating business units, driving accountability, and ensuring acquired companies are successfully embedded into Net at Work's operating model. Rather than simply managing a 60–90 day transition, this role remains engaged until integration objectives have been achieved and the business is operating independently within Net at Work's standards, processes, systems, and culture.

Working closely with executive leadership, Finance, Operations, IT, People & Learning (Human Resources), Customer Success, Sales, Legal, Marketing, and Professional Services, the Manager drives execution of integration plans while proactively identifying risks, removing roadblocks, and ensuring strategic initiatives remain on schedule. The ideal candidate thrives in fast-paced, high-growth environments, possesses exceptional organizational and communication skills, and can influence leaders across the organization without direct reporting authority.

Job Responsibilities



- Partner with executive sponsors to establish integration priorities, timelines, and success criteria.
- Develop comprehensive integration roadmaps, work plans, milestone schedules, risk registers, issue logs, dependency trackers, and executive status reports.
- Support integration planning during due diligence by identifying operational requirements and potential risks before close.
- Manage relationships with acquired leadership teams and sellers throughout the integration lifecycle, serving as the primary operational point of contact.
- Build strong partnerships across the organization and foster a collaborative, solutions-oriented integration culture.
- Lead operational integration activities from the completion of initial customer onboarding through long-term operational stabilization for multiple acquisitions simultaneously.
- Coordinate cross-functional workstreams across Financial Operations, IT, Infrastructure, People & Learning, Operations, Customer Success, Sales Operations, Marketing, Procurement, and Legal.
- Coordinate organizational transitions, policy alignment, and change management activities.
- Coordinate billing conversions, ERP transitions, CRM alignment, reporting, and operational process standardization.
- Coordinate technology migrations including user access, infrastructure, security, collaboration tools, and business applications.
- Partner with Finance on purchase agreement obligations including earnouts, APA holdbacks, Due To/Due From reconciliations, and financial integration activities.
- Identify operational, financial, technology, customer, and organizational risks and recommend mitigation strategies.
- Drive accountability by facilitating recurring integration meetings and ensuring action items are completed on time.
- Prepare executive dashboards and regularly communicate integration progress, accomplishments, risks, and decisions requiring leadership support.
- Document lessons learned following each acquisition and continuously improve integration playbooks, governance models, templates, and best practices.
- Ensure ownership is successfully transitioned to business leaders only after integration objectives have been achieved.

Job Requirements



- Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, Project Management, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
- 5–8+ years of experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives, integration programs, PMO, consulting, business transformation, or M&A integration.
- Experience managing multiple projects with competing priorities and executive stakeholders.
- Strong analytical, organizational, facilitation, and communication skills.
- Demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority and build credibility across all levels of an organization.
- Technology services, managed services, consulting, SaaS, or private equity-backed experience preferred.
- Experience with project management methodologies and tools; PMP, Lean Six Sigma, or Prosci certification is a plus.

Customer Requirements

This job may require access to customer information, systems, and/or premises. As a result, this job may require customer approval for such access as an essential job function.

Core Competencies



- Client Champion – Relentlessly exceed client expectations. Consistently anticipate needs to deliver valuable solutions and extraordinary outcomes.
- Problem Solver – Smart, analytical, inquisitive, knowledge-seeker that thrives on a challenge.
- Promise Keeper – Place high value on keeping our word and doing the right thing. Demonstrate honesty, integrity, and commitment.
- Collaborative Integrator –Team player, unifier, relationship-oriented, win-win seeker, exemplify the concept of relationships through trust and unity.
- Driven Intrapreneur – Exceed goals using independent creative thinking, optimism, self-confidence, and a can-do attitude.
- Inspiring Coach – Help employees, clients and partners using knowledge, expertise, experience, and situational fluency.

Compensation And Benefits

Base salary range: TBD.

This position is also eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the Company's plan.

Please note that the quoted pay range for this job is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) experience, including industry or product-specific experience, education, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, and/or other applicable laws. 

Benefits

We provide competitive, affordable, and diverse benefit programs that support your total health – from healthy body to healthy mind. These benefits support you and your family in all aspects of life:



- Health and Welfare (Medical, Dental, Vision) 
- Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity 
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP) 
- Life and AD&D Insurance 
- Short- and Long-Term Disability Insurance 
- Flexible Spending Accounts 
- Transportation and Parking Accounts 
- Health Savings Accounts (with company contribution) 
- Retirement Planning (401k with matching contribution) 
- Legal Benefits 
- Identity Theft Protection 
- Pet Insurance 
- Wellness Program Offerings 
- Paid Time Off, accrued per pay period based on years of service starting at 15 days annually. 
- 8 Paid Holidays per year, including 1 floating holiday. 

The compensation and benefits information is accurate of the date of this posting and subject to plan eligibility. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, with or without notice, subject to applicable law.

The Company expects to accept applications for this position until September 19, 2026 but encourages interested applicants to apply as soon as possible. We will review this information and one of our Talent Acquisition professionals will reach out if your background aligns to the positions.

EOE/Diversity & Inclusion Statement

Net at Work is dedicated to unleashing the power and potential of our employees and teams by creating a vibrant and inclusive workplace where each employee can be their best. We are committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of diversity and inclusion. We embrace and encourage equitable treatment of our employees and strive to create a work environment free of discrimination at all organizational levels and in all forms. Net at Work recognizes the rights of all individuals to mutual respect and the acceptance of others without biases based on differences of any kind.

Net at Work is a proud equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fair hiring practices and to creating a welcoming environment for all team members that is free of discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions at Net at Work are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications without regard to race, color, religion or belief, family or parental status, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, veteran or disability status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.

Overview

Baker Tilly is a leading advisory, tax and assurance firm, providing clients with a genuine coast-to-coast and global advantage in major regions of the U.S. and in many of the world’s leading financial centers – New York, London, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Chicago and Boston. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and Baker Tilly US, LLP (Baker Tilly) provide professional services through an alternative practice structure in accordance with the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct and applicable laws, regulations and professional standards. Baker Tilly US, LLP is a licensed independent CPA firm that provides attest services to its clients. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and its subsidiary entities provide tax and business advisory services to their clients. Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and its subsidiary entities are not licensed CPA firms.

Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP and Baker Tilly US, LLP, trading as Baker Tilly, are independent members of Baker Tilly International, a worldwide network of independent accounting and business advisory firms in 141 territories, with 43,000 professionals and a combined worldwide revenue of $5.2 billion. Visit bakertilly.com or join the conversation on LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram.

Please discuss the work location status with your Baker Tilly talent acquisition professional to understand the requirements for an opportunity you are exploring.

Baker Tilly is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability or protected veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected basis, in accordance with applicable federal, state or local law.

Any unsolicited resumes submitted through our website or to Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, employee e-mail accounts are considered property of Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, and are not subject to payment of agency fees. In order to be an authorized recruitment agency ("search firm") for Baker Tilly Advisory Group, LP, there must be a formal written agreement in place and the agency must be invited, by Baker Tilly's Talent Attraction team, to submit candidates for review via our applicant tracking system.

Job Description

The M&A Integration Manager is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing the successful integration of acquired CPA and professional services firms. This role serves as the central project leader from Letter of Intent (LOI) through post-close integration, ensuring acquired firms are successfully transitioned into the organization's people, processes, technology, and culture.

Working closely with Corporate Development, Executive Leadership, Finance, HR, IT, Operations, Marketing, Practice Leadership, and external partners, the M&A Integration Manager drives integration planning, governance, execution, and continuous improvement while minimizing disruption to clients and team members.

The ideal candidate is an exceptional project manager who thrives in a fast-paced, acquisition-driven environment and can influence stakeholders across multiple functions without direct authority.

Responsibilities

Integration Leadership

Duties

Lead end-to-end post-merger integration activities across multiple concurrent acquisitions, developing and managing detailed integration workplans, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, and timelines. Coordinate integration activities from pre-close planning through operational stabilization. Support transition from due diligence to post-close execution, ensuring consistent execution of the firm’s Integration Playbook. Duties include:

Project Management



- Facilitate recurring integration meetings and executive steering committees.
- Monitor project health, timelines, risks, and dependencies.
- Maintain project dashboards and executive reporting.
- Escalate critical issues with recommended solutions.
- Manage multiple acquisitions simultaneously.
- Ensure accountability for deliverables while proactively identifying risks and removing roadblocks.

Change Management



- Support acquired firm leaders throughout the integration journey.
- Promote effective communication and organizational change.
- Assist with onboarding and orientation activities.
- Help preserve client relationships while integrating operational processes.
- Foster adoption of firm standards, systems, and best practices.

Stakeholder Communication

Serve as the primary integration contact for acquired firms.

Build trusted relationships with partners and firm leadership.

Prepare executive presentations, status updates, and reporting.

Communicate project progress, risks, and accomplishments to leadership.

Continuous Improvement

Process Improvement



- Continuously improve integration methodologies, templates, and playbooks.
- Capture lessons learned after each acquisition.
- Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability, and consistency.
- Support development of integration KPIs and performance metrics.

Cross-Functional Coordination



- Partner with functional leaders to coordinate integration and ongoing process improvement across:

- Human Resources
- Information Technology
- Finance & Accounting
- Operations
- Marketing & Business Development
- Risk Management
- Practice Management
- Facilities
- Learning & Development
Qualifications



- Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Management, or related field required
- 5+ years of experience leading complex cross-functional projects.
- Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously.
- Strong organizational and project management skills.
- Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
- Ability to influence stakeholders without direct authority.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
- Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and Project or comparable project management software.
- Experience within a CPA firm, consulting firm, or professional services organization required.
- Experience supporting mergers and acquisitions or post-merger integration.
- PMP, CAPM, Prosci Change Management, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certification a plus.
- Familiarity with Smartsheet, Monday.com, Asana, Jira, or Microsoft Project required.
- Experience with CRM, ERP, HRIS, or practice management platforms a plus

The pay rate range for this job position are listed below. Actual compensation is influenced by a variety of relevant factors including but not limited to applicant’s skills, prior experience, qualifications, degrees, professional certifications, work arrangements and geographic location. Baker Tilly offers a comprehensive compensation and benefits package to eligible employees.

The national pay rate range is $98,230 to $186,220

opportunity.job_description:
Compensation: $100,000 – $125,000+ + 10% Bonus

Location: Remote/Hybrid | Approximately 50% Travel

Why This Construction Integration Manager Opportunity Stands Out

This Construction Integration Manager opportunity offers the chance to join a rapidly growing, PE-backed construction platform expanding through acquisitions. The Construction Integration Manager will play a key role in bringing newly acquired businesses into the broader organization, partnering across operations, finance, procurement, and technology to create consistent and scalable processes.

What Makes This Construction Integration Manager Opportunity Especially Compelling



- Join a PE-backed construction platform experiencing significant acquisition-driven growth
- Play a hands-on role integrating newly acquired construction and roofing businesses
- Gain direct exposure to the CFO and executive leadership
- Work across operations, finance, accounting, procurement, technology, and field leadership
- Influence integration strategy, operating procedures, systems, and best practices
- Gain significant exposure to M&A and post-acquisition integration
- Competitive compensation plus 10% bonus
- Strong career advancement potential as the organization continues to acquire and scale

This role is ideal for someone who understands how construction businesses actually operate and can combine that knowledge with process improvement, financial acumen, systems implementation, and acquisition integration.

Key Responsibilities of the Construction Integration Manager



- Lead post-acquisition integration efforts for newly acquired roofing, construction, and related operating businesses
- Conduct operational assessments to identify integration priorities, process gaps, risks, and opportunities
- Partner with field leadership to understand existing business processes and develop practical integration plans
- Coordinate across Finance, Accounting, Operations, Procurement, and executive leadership to standardize processes
- Support operational and financial due diligence surrounding acquisition and integration activities
- Assist with implementation and adoption of ERP, CRM, reporting, and other business systems
- Develop standardized workflows, reporting structures, controls, and operating procedures
- Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, visibility, compliance, and consistency across acquired businesses
- Track integration milestones and ensure key initiatives remain on schedule
- Travel directly to operating companies to support onboarding, training, system implementation, and change management
- Provide leadership with updates regarding integration progress, challenges, and recommended solutions

As the Construction Integration Manager, this individual will serve as an important bridge between newly acquired businesses and corporate leadership.

Qualifications For The Construction Integration Manager



- Experience within construction, roofing, building services, specialty contracting, or a closely related industry required
- Experience supporting acquisitions, post-acquisition integrations, multi-location transformations, or business integration initiatives
- Strong understanding of construction operations and how field-based businesses operate
- Background combining operations with finance, accounting, financial analysis, or business process improvement
- Experience with ERP, CRM, financial reporting, or other enterprise business systems
- Experience standardizing processes across multiple locations or operating businesses
- Ability to work cross-functionally with field operations, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, IT, and executive leadership
- Ability and willingness to travel approximately 50%
- Must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship requirements

Benefits & Growth



- Exposure to an active acquisition and integration strategy
- Direct interaction with executive leadership
- Opportunity to develop deep M&A and post-acquisition integration experience
- Significant influence over processes and systems as the organization scales
- Long-term advancement into broader integration or operational leadership opportunities

Who This Construction Integration Manager Role Is Built For

The ideal Construction Integration Manager isn't purely a finance professional or a traditional project manager. This person understands the operational side of construction or roofing and can walk into an acquired business, understand how it operates, identify gaps, and help transition it into a larger platform. Construction, roofing, or related building-services industry experience required.

opportunity.job_description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Finance M&A Integration & Analysis Manager based in the United States.

This role plays a key part in supporting a growing acquisition strategy by leading finance integration activities across newly acquired businesses. You’ll operate at the intersection of M&A due diligence, financial planning, integration execution, and post-acquisition performance management. The position offers broad exposure across Finance, Accounting, IT, Data & Analytics, Operations, and external advisors. You’ll help ensure acquired businesses transition effectively into established financial, reporting, and operational environments. The role combines financial modeling, analytical problem-solving, project leadership, and strategic thinking in a fast-paced environment. You’ll also help develop repeatable integration processes and best practices as acquisition activity expands. It’s an opportunity for an M&A-focused finance professional to have a direct impact on both transaction success and long-term business performance.

Accountabilities



- Support M&A due diligence: Review financial information, operational metrics, business assumptions, and forecasts for prospective acquisitions, helping assess opportunities, risks, and potential synergies.
- Prepare pre-close integration plans: Evaluate target financial data structures, charts of accounts, reporting frameworks, and other requirements to establish effective integration plans before transaction close.
- Lead finance integration: Manage finance-related integration activities for acquired businesses, coordinating the transition of financial data, reporting structures, budgeting processes, and other core finance capabilities.
- Coordinate systems and data migration: Partner with Accounting, IT, Data & Analytics, Operations, and other stakeholders to facilitate system conversions, data migration, and alignment with enterprise processes.
- Support purchase accounting: Coordinate with internal teams and external advisors to support purchase accounting activities and ensure appropriate financial integration.
- Establish performance reporting: Develop reporting processes, KPIs, and performance metrics for newly acquired businesses to provide visibility into post-acquisition results.
- Track synergies and acquisition performance: Build and maintain synergy tracking, monitor performance against investment theses and forecast assumptions, and identify opportunities or risks requiring action.
- Develop executive reporting: Prepare post-acquisition business reviews, financial analyses, and executive-level reporting that support decision-making and performance management.
- Support earn-out analysis: Assist with earn-out calculations, performance monitoring, and related financial analyses.
- Drive strategic finance projects: Lead or support special initiatives involving process improvement, reporting enhancements, operational scalability, and evolving business priorities.
- Build scalable integration practices: Develop repeatable methodologies, tools, and best practices that improve the efficiency and consistency of future acquisition integrations.

Requirements



- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field is required.
- Professional experience: At least 5 years of progressive experience in finance, FP&A, corporate development, M&A integration, or a closely related discipline.
- M&A expertise: Demonstrated experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, business integrations, or post-close integration activities.
- Financial analysis: Advanced financial modeling, analytical, forecasting, and problem-solving capabilities.
- Integration experience: Ability to coordinate financial data, reporting structures, systems, budgeting processes, and performance management across organizations.
- Cross-functional leadership: Strong ability to collaborate with Finance, Accounting, IT, Data & Analytics, Operations, external advisors, and senior stakeholders.
- Project management: Ability to manage complex initiatives from planning through execution while balancing multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Strategic thinking: Ability to assess risks, opportunities, synergies, and business performance and translate findings into practical recommendations.
- Preferred experience: Background in a private equity-backed organization or professional services environment is advantageous.
- Functional breadth: Exposure to both FP&A and accounting functions, as well as post-close reporting and business integration, is preferred.
- Technology: Familiarity with Workday ERP platforms is a plus.
- Advanced credentials: An MBA, CPA, or other relevant advanced business qualification is preferred but not required.
- Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present financial insights clearly to executives and cross-functional stakeholders.

Benefits



- Estimated base salary range of $117,000–$158,000, with actual compensation determined by factors including location, skills, experience, education, certifications, business needs, and applicable employment requirements.
- Eligibility for an annual discretionary bonus based on applicable participation rules and individual and organizational performance.
- Eight health plan options, including HMO and PPO choices.
- Dental and vision coverage.
- Health Savings Account (HSA) eligibility with potential employer contribution.
- Employee Assistance Program.
- Employer-sponsored basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage.
- 401(k) savings plan with profit sharing and employer matching contributions.
- Well-being incentive programs.
- Education and professional certification assistance.
- Flexible time off.
- Family care and parental leave.
- Family formation benefits.
- Cell phone reimbursement.
- Travel rewards.
- Voluntary benefits including critical illness and accident insurance, hospital indemnity, legal services, long-term care, pet insurance, identity theft protection, and supplemental life/AD&D coverage.
- Remote work flexibility.
- Opportunities to work on high-impact M&A initiatives and collaborate across finance, technology, operations, and advisory functions.
- Benefits eligibility varies based on annual hours, position status and level, and work location.

opportunity.job_title: Manager Operations Escrow - Market Street Settlement Group LLC- Remote Northeast Region
opportunity.job_description:
Job Description

The Regional Operations Support Manager is a strategic partner dedicated to optimizing and supporting operational processes for escrow teams across multiple brands and states within assigned region. This role focuses on driving operational excellence, process standardization, and technology integration, while providing expert guidance and support to branch and regional escrow teams. This role collaborates closely with senior leadership, the National Operations Center, and cross-functional partners to ensure every operational touchpoint reflects the company’s values, vision, and commitment to service excellence.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Support & Process Optimization



-  Analyze, refine, and standardize operational processes to increase efficiency and productivity for escrow assistants and closers in customer-facing roles. 
-  Collaborate with the National Operations Center (NOC) to develop and integrate standardized workflows between NOC and branches. 
-  Monitor and analyze operational KPIs to identify trends, drive performance, and implement improvements. 
-  Provide guidance, training, and support to regional escrow support departments, ensuring high team performance and job satisfaction. 

Claims Management & Risk Mitigation



-  Support escrow teams in the identification, resolution, and prevention of title claims. 
-  Implement proactive risk management strategies and ensure regulatory compliance in partnership with legal and underwriting teams. 

Strategic Program Development



-  Design and execute regional initiatives to enhance efficiency, profitability, and customer experience for escrow operations. 
-  Pilot innovative programs using a test-and-learn approach, iterating based on data and feedback. 

Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement



-  Work closely with cross-functional teams, including sales, customer service, finance, compliance, and technology, to integrate process improvements and enhance customer satisfaction. 
-  Act as a resource and escalation point for regional leaders and branch teams. 

Technology Integration & Innovation



-  Champion adoption and integration of technology platforms to streamline escrow operations and improve customer experience. 
-  Support IT in developing or improving technology platforms used to close transactions. 
-  Evaluate and implement new technologies, including BOTs, AI tools, workflow dashboards, and reporting systems, to improve efficiency and accuracy. 
-  Utilize data analytics to uncover trends, track KPIs, and inform strategic initiatives. 

Training & Documentation



-  Develop comprehensive training programs to ensure staff proficiency in optimized processes. 
-  Maintain thorough documentation of operational procedures and updates. 
-  Foster a culture of teamwork, customer service, and continuous improvement. 

Requirements



-  5+ years in title and escrow operations with multi-state oversight preferred. 
-  Proven expertise in operational support, process optimization, and risk mitigation.

Job Description

The Regional Operations Support Manager is a strategic partner dedicated to optimizing and supporting operational processes for escrow teams across multiple brands and states within assigned region. This role collaborates closely with senior leadership, the National Operations Center, and cross-functional partners to ensure every operational touchpoint reflects the company’s values, vision, and commitment to service excellence.

-  Analyze, refine, and standardize operational processes to increase efficiency and productivity for escrow assistants and closers in customer-facing roles. 
-  Collaborate with the National Operations Center (NOC) to develop and integrate standardized workflows between NOC and branches. 
-  Monitor and analyze operational KPIs to identify trends, drive performance, and implement improvements. 
-  Provide guidance, training, and support to regional escrow support departments, ensuring high team performance and job satisfaction.

-  Support escrow teams in the identification, resolution, and prevention of title claims.

For our client, we are seeking a Corporate Development Manager to join the team of a leader in the Healthcare space. This role will drive strategic priorities, executive-level problem solving, and cross-functional execution on initiatives that matter most to the business. You will partner with senior leaders and teams across the organization to clarify priorities, coordinate complex work, and turn strategic decisions into measurable action. The position offers the opportunity to strengthen operating cadence, decision quality, and enterprise execution within a healthcare environment.

Location: Remote - US based candidates only, no visa sponsorship available

Compensation: $120,000 – $147,000 annually

Responsibilities



-  Manage data collection and analysis for acquisitions
-  Conduct market research and competitive analysis for growth initiatives
-  Cultivate relationships with M&A stakeholders and influencers
-  Perform financial and operational due diligence
-  Draft and review legal documentation for deal execution
-  Collaborate with cross-functional teams for transaction integrations
-  Maintain relationships with financial partners to track market dynamics

Qualifications



-  Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business, Economics, or related field
-  5+ years in corporate development, investment banking, management consulting, or private equity, preferably in healthcare
-  Experience in financial modeling, M&A execution, and strategic planning
-  Strong analytical, negotiation, and project management abilities
-  Proven ability to present and influence senior executives effectively
-  Attention to detail with high integrity in handling confidential information
-  Proficient in Excel and PowerPoint; familiarity with corporate finance

Benefits



-  Supportive work environment promoting teamwork and cultural alignment
-  Opportunities for professional development and growth
-  Annual bonus potential based on performance
-  Exposure to strategic projects in a growing healthcare sector
-  Access to advanced AI tools for improved analysis and workflow efficiency

Our client is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification—your background could be exactly what this team needs.

opportunity.job_description:
At Wipfli, people count.

At Wipfli, our people are core to everything we do—the catalyst behind our ability to create exceptional impact and extraordinary results.

We believe in flexibility. We focus on relationships. We encourage each individual to follow their own path.

People truly matter and they feel it. For those looking to make a difference and find a professional home, Wipfli offers a career-defining opportunity.

Job Summary: In this role, you will perform comprehensive financial analysis, collaborate with the team to evaluate deal structures, and stay updated on industry trends to provide valuable insights for our clients. You will manage multiple projects simultaneously, act as a key point of contact for clients, and work closely with cross-functional teams to enhance the overall value provided. Additionally, you will prepare clear and concise reports, review the work of junior team members, and ensure the highest standards of quality and accuracy in all deliverables.

Responsibilities



- Perform comprehensive financial analysis, including historical and projected financial statements, to assess the target company's performance and identify potential risks and opportunities.
- Collaborate with the team to evaluate deal structures and valuation methodologies, considering factors such as market conditions, industry trends, and specific transaction characteristics.
- Stay updated on industry trends, market dynamics, and competitive landscapes to provide valuable insights that contribute to the client's decision-making process.
- Manage and prioritize multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring timely delivery of high-quality work products and meeting client expectations.
- Act as a key point of contact for clients, building strong relationships and effectively communicating findings and recommendations.
- Work closely with cross-functional teams to leverage expertise from other practice areas, enhancing the overall value provided to clients.
- Prepare clear and concise reports and presentations that communicate complex financial information in a digestible manner for clients and internal stakeholders.
- Review and verify the work of junior team members to maintain the highest standards of quality and accuracy in all deliverables.

Qualifications And Experience



- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
- 5+ years of experience in Transaction Advisory Services or related areas.
- Strong financial modeling and analysis skills, with proficiency in Excel and financial databases.
- Excellent understanding of financial statements, valuation techniques, and deal structuring.
- Demonstrated ability to manage projects and deliver results within strict timelines.
- Outstanding communication skills, both written and verbal, to effectively interact with clients and team members.
- Proven problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities with a keen eye for detail.
- Familiarity with industry-specific regulations and compliance standards (e.g., IFRS, GAAP) is advantageous.
- Professional certifications such as CPA or CFA are desirable but not mandatory

Tiffany Farnsworth, from our recruiting team, will be guiding you through this process. Visit her LinkedIn page to connect!

Additional Details

Wipfli is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All candidates will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identify, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristics protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Wipfli is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete an application, interview, or participate in our recruiting process, please send us an email at hr@wipfli.com

Wipfli values fair, transparent, and competitive compensation, considering each candidate's unique skills and experiences. The estimated base pay range for this role is $117,000 to $158,000, with offers typically not made at the maximum, allowing for future salary increases. The actual salary at the time of offer depends on business related factors like location, skills, experience, training/education, licensure, certifications, business needs, current associate pay, and relevant employment laws.

Individuals may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, subject to participation rules and based on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual and Firm performance.

Wipfli cares about our associates and offers a variety of benefits to support their well-being. Highlights include 8 health plan options (both HMO & PPO plans), dental and vision coverage, opportunity to enroll in HSA with potential Firm contribution and an Employee Assistance Program. Other benefits include firm-sponsored basic life and short and long-term disability coverage, a 401(k) savings plan & profit share as well as Firm matching contribution, well-being incentive, education & certification assistance, flexible time off, family care leave, parental leave, family formation benefits, cell phone reimbursement, and travel rewards. Voluntary benefit offerings include critical illness & accident insurance, hospital indemnity insurance, legal, long-term care, pet insurance, ID theft protection, and supplemental life/AD&D. Eligibility for all benefits programs is dependent on annual hours expectation, position status/level and location.

opportunity.job_description:
Senior Insolvency Accountant


One of our clients is currently seeking a Senior Insolvency Accountant to join their business recovery unit based in Sydney. This role will provide you with an opportunity to develop and hone your insolvency skills as you assist clients through corporate distress, voluntary liquidations, restructurings and administrations. The role would suit someone who has had exposure to conducting specialist insolvency processes and is able to demonstrate good attention to detail.


This is a unique opportunity for someone looking to take their accountancy career in a different direction. The role offers fantastic support in terms of training and development and uncapped progression, making it the perfect position for an ambitious accountant who wants to develop their career with the benefit of working for a prestigious firm.


We are looking for a talented professional with between 2 to 4 years’ relevant experience. You will gain valuable hands-on commercial experience as a key member of the team with the opportunity to learn from seasoned professionals and alongside experienced client management teams.


What You’ll Do:

- Work in a supportive environment fostering integrity, creativity, achievement, respect, and empathy
- Manage day-to-day issues on formal insolvency engagements, including trade-on management, receipts and payments and assist in stakeholder communication both written and verbal
- Assist in non-formal engagements, including independent business reviews and informal turnaround assignments
- Prepare draft reports, presentations and other written correspondence
- Conduct financial analysis and prepare estimated outcome positions for formal insolvency matters
- Be a supportive key team member on all engagements
- Perform financial, ratio and company analysis and financial and cash flow modelling
- Be a key member involved in various business development initiatives


To apply you must have:

- 2-4 years of professional restructuring/insolvency experience
- Tertiary qualifications in an accounting or finance related field
- Studying Chartered Accounting (CA) program or be CA qualified or the equivalent
- Driven to deliver high quality client service
- With strong attention to detail Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
- Strong financial analytical and quantitative skills
- Knowledge of fundamental accounting and business/commercial principles
- Proficiency with the Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint


To be successful in this role you will need to have some exposure to the above duties in a previous insolvency role (highly desirable), and be ready to step up into a more autonomous role, as part of a large team.

opportunity.job_description:
About Us


At Stress Free Accounts, we do exactly what our name says. We look after small businesses, SMSFs, and individuals across Port Stephens and Newcastle, without the usual stress.


One of our long-term team members is heading into retirement, and we're looking for someone great to step into their shoes in our Medowie office. They've been a fantastic, trusted part of our team for years and we're after someone with that same warmth and "get it done" spirit to carry that on.


We'd love someone with plenty of experience, but we're just as keen to hear from the right person with 5+ years who's ready for the next step up.




The Role


We trust our senior accountants to genuinely own their work. You'll run your own portfolio of clients your way, backed by a Director and team who are always happy to jump in when you want them to. Plus we cover all your ongoing CPD costs, so you're always learning and improving.


You'll be doing the interesting stuff- complex tax returns, financial statements, business advisory, client relationship management, as well as mentoring our juniors and working closely with the Director on where the business is heading. There's real room to grow, too: build and manage your own client base, and enjoy our bonus structure to reward you for it.


We're keen to get someone started as soon as possible, so there's plenty of time for a proper handover and to meet the clients before our current team member heads off.




What we're looking for:


• 5+ years experience in public practice
• Comfortable running a client list from start to finish
• Familiar with our tech stack — Xero, Xero Practice Manager, Xero Tax, Xero Workpapers, and Claude (or keen to get up to speed)
• Genuinely good with people — our clients are locals who love a real conversation, not just a set of numbers
• Good grounding in complex tax scenarios — CGT, FBT, business structuring
• Comfortable handling tax returns and financial statements for individuals, companies, partnerships and trusts
• Takes real pride in getting the details right




What's in it for you?


• Salary: $115k – $135k + Super, depending on the experience you bring
• Work/Life Balance: We mean it. 5 days, 4 days, or a 9-day fortnight — happy to work around what suits you
• Flexibility: 2 days WFH. We're also moving towards a more online, virtual way of working over time — the Medowie office stays as our base for the team and client meetings, but you won't be chained to a desk
• Tech: A genuinely modern, cloud-based setup — no clunky legacy systems to fight with
• The Environment: A small welcoming office in Medowie with a team that genuinely gets along. We're straight talkers here — no politics, no ego, just honest conversations with each other and our clients




How to Apply


If you're looking for a stable, long-term role where you're trusted, supported, and genuinely valued for your expertise, we'd love to hear from you.

opportunity.job_description:
Location: Perth, WA, AU, 6000

Company: McGrathNicol

Division: Advisory

Department: Forensic

Employment Type: Full Time Permanent

Application Closing Date: 31 Dec 2026

About Us

McGrathNicol is an independent professional services firm specialising in Cyber, Deals, Forensic, Performance, Restructuring, and Risk & Compliance. For more than 20 years, we have supported organisations to navigate critical moments, from growth and transformation through to financial stress and uncertainty, across the private, public and not-for-profit sectors. Guided by our values – Understanding, Commitment and Impact – we are client-focused, collaborative and committed to creating an environment where our people can do their best work and continue to grow their careers.

The Opportunity

Working with nationally and internationally recognised forensic accounting experts, you will help courts, clients and their legal advisers navigate the financial aspects of commercial disputes, providing impartial advice and practical solutions to achieve the best possible outcomes.

You will be involved in building client relationships and pursuing opportunities, delivering clear and technically sound solutions on an interesting array of assignments, and driving continuous improvement in the quality and efficiency of deliverables and client service. An excellent career path is on offer with plenty of room to grow.

Key Responsibilities



- Plan and deliver a range of forensic and advisory assignments, with an emphasis on dispute advisory and business valuation services.
- Contribute to the preparation of independent expert reports and supporting financial models for dispute resolution purposes.
- Quantify economic loss, damages and other remedies in the context of commercial disputes.
- Perform valuations of businesses, shares and other equity, intellectual property and other intangible assets.
- Review and critique the work of other expert accountants and valuers in legal proceedings.
- Undertake company, industry and other financial analysis.
- Maintain compliance with professional and risk management processes.
- Participate in business development, including relationship development and opportunity research.

About You



- A relevant undergraduate degree (e.g. commerce, finance, business, economics, law). Ideally hold or be working towards a relevant professional qualification (Chartered Accountant or Chartered Financial Analyst) or have an interest in obtaining one.
- Relevant professional experience, which may include forensic accounting, corporate finance, insolvency, audit, tax or other advisory services (dispute advisory and valuations experience will be highly regarded).
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint, ideally with experience in building financial models including discounted cash flow analyses (familiarity with S&P Capital IQ will also be highly regarded).
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Excellent presentation, problem-solving and analytical skills, with exceptional attention to detail.
- Strong business and commercial acumen.

Why Join Us?

At McGrathNicol, you’ll thrive in an empowering environment where your expertise drives real impact. We offer a competitive annual bonus program, alongside exceptional training and career development opportunities. Our inclusive culture fosters growth through personalised mentorship. You’ll also benefit from comprehensive support such as 26 weeks parental leave, additional leave options, employee assistance, health and wellbeing programs, and opportunities for social and community engagement. Join us and be part of a team that values your contributions and supports your success.

Interested?

To apply for this exciting opportunity please click ‘Apply’ below. If you would like further information, please contact our HR team via HR@mcgrathnicol.com.

opportunity.job_description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

Senior Manager or Manager - Forensics and Integrity Services - Claims and Dispute

The opportunity

As a Senior Manager or Manager within the Forensics & Integrity Services (FIS) team you will be working on high-profile disputes, forensic accounting investigations and contentious quantifications, and regulatory matters in one of the most exciting areas of professional services. Working with clients across all industries, you’ll build valued relationships with external clients and internal peers and develop a portfolio of projects by focusing on high value opportunities in complex forensic accounting analysis and dispute related engagements. You will work alongside an experienced leadership group that is focused on driving growth in the market. EY’s FIS professionals help organisations protect and restore enterprise and financial reputation. We assist organisations to investigate facts, resolve disputes and manage regulatory challenges, ethical and reputational risks.

You will be part of a multi-disciplinary Oceania FIS team including accountants, risk managers, technology specialists and former regulatory and law enforcement professionals.

This is a hybrid position based in Naarm – Melbourne. Our roles can potentially be adjusted to work flexibly with reduced hours. Please speak with us about potential options.

Your Key Responsibilities



- Lead and deliver a range of forensic accounting and disputes engagements, including investigations, commercial disputes, post-acquisition disputes, and independent expert matters.
- Perform and oversee financial analysis, document reviews, and reporting activities.
- Work closely with clients to understand complex forensic accounting issues and deliver high-quality outcomes.
- Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including corporate clients, legal advisers, insurers, and internal senior leaders.
- Prepare and review forensic accounting, investigation, dispute-related, and expert witness reports.
- Support, coach, and develop team members while contributing to the growth and success of the Forensics & Integrity Services team

Skills And Attributes For Success



- CA ANZ (or equivalent) qualification.
- Experience in forensic accounting, external audit, disputes, investigations, or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience working within a professional services environment.
- Strong client service skills with the ability to build and maintain trusted stakeholder relationships.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively.
- Adaptable and resilient, with the ability to navigate changing priorities and manage competing demands.
- Advanced proficiency in Excel, including experience with financial analysis and financial modelling.
- Experience leading or mentoring team members and contributing to a collaborative team culture.

Ideally, you’ll also have the skills and attributes below but don’t worry if you don’t tick all the boxes. We’re interested in your aptitude, attitude and willingness to learn.



- Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with a commitment to continuous professional development.
- Excellent report writing skills and strong attention to detail.

What We Offer You

At EY, we’ll fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive culture of globally connected teams. We’re proud to be recognised as the #1 WORK180 Endorsed Employer in the Top 101 Employers for Women 2026. Learn more.



- Career development: At EY, your career is yours to shape! We’ll develop you with future-focused skills and equip you with world-class experiences com/au/careerdevelopment
- Flexible work arrangements: Our flexible work policies empower you to balance your professional and personal life, fostering a culture of trust and autonomy.
- A comprehensive benefits package: From a yearly wellness incentive, to access to additional 8 weeks of flex leave per year, and family-friendly policies, including 26 weeks of gender-neutral paid parental leave, we cater to your diverse needs to help you thrive both personally and professionally www.ey.com/au/benefits 
- Salary: We offer a competitive salary which is open to negotiation pending on skills and experience.

Acknowledgement of Country

EY acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Custodians of the lands on which EY offices are located around Australia. We pay our respects to their cultures, and to their Elders — past, present, and emerging. Find out more about our vision for reconciliation at ey.com/en_au/careers/indigenous

Inclusiveness is core to who we are and how we work together, driving value for our people and for our business. opportunity.job_title: Forensic Commercial - Senior Accountant or Manager
opportunity.job_description:
Grow with us. Shape what’s next. 


At Vincents, we’re not your typical professional services firm. We’re a team of curious, collaborative professionals who want to use our expertise to make a real difference - for our clients, our colleagues, and our communities. With deep capability across Forensic, Tax, and Advisory, we help businesses navigate complexity, make smart decisions, and thrive.
Our vision is simple: to be the trusted advisors of choice - where people thrive and clients succeed.


Why this role matters 
Our team offer expert support across a range of legal disputes and financial investigations. We have long been recognised as trusted experts in forensic accounting and litigation support, providing opinion evidence of the highest quality and reliability. We continue to experience growth and are looking for an analytically minded and client focused Senior Accountant or Manager (Associate) seeking exposure to a wide variety of interesting and challenging engagements, working alongside leading forensic accountants who will support you to become an expert in the field


What you’ll do

- Critically analyse financial and non-financial information to understand business and industry drivers
- Following this analysis, undertaking business valuations and assessing economic loss claims
- Conduct additional real-time financial and economic research across a variety of businesses and industries, as required
- Analysis of large data sets and manipulation through the development of financial models
- Preparation of expert reports for use as evidence in Court proceedings and pre-litigation matters
- Communication with internal and external stakeholders, specifically those within the legal industry
- Excellent opportunity to build a career path within the forensic accounting industry.


What you’ll bring

- CA or CPA accreditation (or in progress)
- Minimum 3 years of proven professional experience in either business and tax advisory, with exposure to business analysis, business valuations, and/or commercial litigation
- Strong business acumen, inquisitive mind and genuine passion for the work you do will see you highly rewarded for your contribution to our team
- An ability to think critically and analytically, with high attention to detail
- Well-developed verbal and written communication, conscious that much of our work is used as evidence in Court proceedings
- Exceptional time management skills which will assist you in meeting client deadlines, often dictated by the Court
- A self-motivation that sees you balance working autonomously and as part of a team.


The Vincents Experience 
We believe people do their best work when they’re supported, challenged, and inspired. That’s why we’ve built a culture where you can grow – and stay.
Here’s what you can expect:

- Hybrid and Flexible working – work in ways that support your life
- VinDay – an extra day of leave to spend however you like
- Monthly 1:1s to guide your growth and development
- Generous support for study memberships, qualifications, and ongoing professional development
- Competitive employee and client referral incentives
- A culture that truly celebrates success – from peer recognition to our annual Values Awards Gala
- An active calendar of social, inclusion, and wellbeing events that bring our people together


Ready to make your mark? Discover more about our expertise and culture at www.vincents.com.au


Don't meet every requirement? We value potential and commitment to continuous improvement over perfect credentials.

Job Description

Are you ready to start your career in Restructuring & Insolvency?

William Buck, more than advisors: We understand that exceptional advice comes from passionate people who thrive in an environment where they feel empowered to shape outcomes. That's why at William Buck, we've created what we like to call the 'Goldilocks' model – a top ten performing business that's just the right size to ensure every employee has a tangible impact.

William Buck is the perfect place to start, grow or take your career to the next level. Be part of a dynamic team that prides itself on delivering advice that makes a diﬀerence.

Description of the role: We’re seeking a 2026 graduate to join our Restructuring & Insolvency team in 2027. In this role you’ll work with businesses facing ﬁnancial challenges, crafting innovative solutions to restore stability and drive positive change. You’ll gain hands-on experience in business turnaround, risk analysis, and stakeholder management.

We are thrilled to be ranked as Prosple’s Top Graduate Employer in the Accounting and Advisory sector for 2025! Additionally, we are proud to have placed in the Top 100 Graduate Employers list for 2025!

What makes you ‘just right’:



- You have completed/are completing a Bachelor’s degree in Business or a similar discipline with a major in Accounting or you have completed a Bachelor's degree in Law
- You have a desire to further your education by pursuing CA and ARITA qualifications – we’ll support this with financial assistance and mentoring opportunities
- You’re detail oriented, eager to learn and ready to take on new challenges
- You are excited to gain exposure to a diverse range of clients and industries
- You’re comfortable working independently but also communicate effectively and work well in a collaborative team

What your day might look like:



- Prepare reports for creditors.
- Trade-on management, including preparing of budgets and forecasts.
- Investigating, analysing and reporting on corporate and personal financial affairs.
- Sales of property, plant and equipment.
- Drafting advice to lawyers and assisting with legal proceedings.
- Preparing insolvent trading and voidable transaction recovery actions.
- Liaising with creditors, employees, business owners, agents, lawyers etc.
- Ensuring compliance with statutory and ethical guidelines.
- Internal cash management and record keeping.
- Exposure to many different industries and diverse groups of people.

What makes us ‘just right’:



- Open door policy – 1 on 1 access to Partners & Managers
- You will be included in client meetings, we believe client exposure is essential to your learning and development!
- Clear career pathways and focused learning and development programs - national Graduate College, monthly tax training, CA support and virtual study sessions
- You will be part of a collaborative, social and inclusive culture - we have lots of social events, firm drinks, and regular colleague networking opportunities
- We are Accountants, but we aren't boring! You will learn a lot, you will be challenged, and you will have a lot of fun
- Flexible working to help you balance work and personal responsibilities.
- Career enhancement and development opportunities. 
- Free company provided Salary Continuance insurance
- Bi-Monthly Colleague Lunch
- Dress for your day policy
- Social Club events
- Working in a vibrant and collegiate culture where you as a person, and your contribution is valued

More about us:

William Buck is a leading network of Chartered Accountants and business advisors, established in 1895, with over 140 partners and 1,100 professional staﬀ across 10 oﬃces in Australia and New Zealand, focusing on deeply understanding clients’ needs and tailoring solutions that go beyond traditional accounting and advisory services.

If you want to join a company where friendships are forged and careers made, then come on over to a place that's delivering more than just advice.

Diversity, equity and inclusion statement:

William Buck is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where diverse perspectives are celebrated, and everyone feels valued. 

Prior to the next step in the recruitment process, we welcome you to inform us conﬁdentially if you may require any special accommodations in order to participate fully in our recruitment process.

- You are excited to gain exposure to a diverse range of clients and industries
- You’re comfortable working independently but also communicate effectively and work well in a collaborative team

- Trade-on management, including preparing of budgets and forecasts.
- Investigating, analysing and reporting on corporate and personal financial affairs.
- Sales of property, plant and equipment.
- Drafting advice to lawyers and assisting with legal proceedings.
- Preparing insolvent trading and voidable transaction recovery actions.
- Liaising with creditors, employees, business owners, agents, lawyers etc.
- Ensuring compliance with statutory and ethical guidelines.
- Internal cash management and record keeping.
- Exposure to many different industries and diverse groups of people.

- Open door policy – 1 on 1 access to Partners & Managers
- You will be included in client meetings, we believe client exposure is essential to your learning and development!
- Clear career pathways and focused learning and development programs - national Graduate College, monthly tax training, CA support and virtual study sessions

opportunity.job_description:
- Forensic Accounting Opportunity
- Location: Sydney
- Role type: Full time / Hybrid and Flexible working
At PKF, our purpose is empowering businesses to focus on what they do best.
We are among Australia’s Top 10 business advisory, accounting and assurance providers. Our organisation is proud to be an entrepreneurial and international brand that opens doors to expertise from around the world. We are part of a globally respected family of like-minded, separately owned firms located in over 400 cities.
Within Australia, we have almost 100 partners and 800 talented people across 12 locations. We transform local ambition into global opportunity and global experience into local growth.
The opportunity
This is a unique opportunity for someone looking to build a successful career in Forensic Accounting. As a well-established Forensic Accounting Team, we’re looking for someone to support the Forensic Principal oversee our team whilst advancing your career by gaining exposure to a diverse range of commercial litigation, family law, estate disputes and insurance litigation matters.
The role
Joining this small team is an exciting opportunity to gain a breadth of experience across a range of forensic accounting matters, interaction with clients and the opportunity to take on additional responsibility as your experience grows. You’ll enjoy applying critical thinking and analysis skills identifying relevant insights from financial and non-financial information and demonstrate the ability to report these in a plain speak manner.
You’ll have experience in

- A broad range of forensic accounting matters including: valuations in a litigious context and quantification of loss in commercial litigation and insurance matters;
- Construction of valuations & economic loss modelling for a range of businesses.
- Conducting research and analysis of a variety of business, industry, and economic data/information.
- Drafting reports with interpretation of financial information and calculation methodologies.
The role with suit someone with

- A relevant degree qualification, CA or CPA qualifications.
- An interest in challenging themselves and advancing their career.
- Well-developed written and verbal skills to communicate effectively.
- Strong organisational skills and enjoys the autonomy to manage projects to completion and deadline.
- A commitment to the professional development of others.
- An interest in liaising with and building relationships with clients and referrers on a day-to-day basis.
- An agile approach in adapting to shifting or competing client deadlines.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Suite including Excel and Word and accounting packages such as Xero and MYOB.
- 5+ years' experience in a similar role.
About Us:
At PKF, we create a positive environment that enable our people to feel valued and achieve their full potential. We offer:

- Competitive remuneration package
- Exceptional opportunity for career development and progression
- Dynamic and talented team to work and develop alongside
- Opportunity for secondment in PKF offices overseas
- Flexible work arrangements
- Work/Life balance encouraged
- Friendly culture and team events
- Outstanding study support and training
- Collaborative and inclusive working environment
- Wellbeing initiatives
- Take your birthday off work – on us
- Employee referral cash bonus.
Please apply today by sending your CV and cover letter to our talent acquisition specialist, Georgina Youssef at GYo•••••@pkf.com.au

opportunity.job_description:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

Senior Consultant - Forensics and Integrity Services - Claims and Dispute

The opportunity

As a Senior Consultant within the Forensics & Integrity Services (FIS) team you will be working on high-profile disputes, forensic accounting investigations and contentious quantifications, and regulatory matters in one of the most exciting areas of professional services. Working with clients across all industries, you’ll build valued relationships with external clients and internal peers and develop a portfolio of projects by focusing on high value opportunities in complex forensic accounting analysis and dispute related engagements. You will work alongside an experienced leadership group that is focused on driving growth in the market. EY’s FIS professionals help organisations protect and restore enterprise and financial reputation. We assist organisations to investigate facts, resolve disputes and manage regulatory challenges, ethical and reputational risks.

You will be part of a multi-disciplinary Oceania FIS team including accountants, risk managers, technology specialists and former regulatory and law enforcement professionals.

This is a hybrid position based in Naarm – Melbourne. Our roles can potentially be adjusted to work flexibly with reduced hours. Please speak with us about potential options.

Your Key Responsibilities



- Work collaboratively on a range of forensic accounting and disputes engagements, including investigations, commercial disputes, post-acquisition disputes, and independent expert matters.
- Conduct financial analysis, document reviews, and prepare clear, high-quality reports.
- Partner with clients and stakeholders to address complex forensic accounting and dispute-related issues.
- Build and maintain relationships with clients, legal representatives, insurers, and internal teams.
- Assist in the preparation of forensic accounting, investigation, and expert witness reports.
- Contribute to the ongoing growth and success of the Forensics & Integrity Services team.

Skills And Attributes For Success



- CA ANZ (or equivalent) qualification, or currently working towards completion.
- Experience in forensic accounting, external audit, or a related professional services environment.
- Strong client focus with the ability to build effective relationships with a range of stakeholders.
- Proficiency in Excel and experience working with financial data and models.

Ideally, you’ll also have the skills and attributes below but don’t worry if you don’t tick all the boxes. We’re interested in your aptitude, attitude and willingness to learn.



- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate and influence effectively.
- Adaptable and resilient, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a dynamic environment.
- Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with a commitment to continuous learning and professional development.
- Excellent report writing skills and strong attention to detail.

What We Offer You

At EY, we’ll fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive culture of globally connected teams. We’re proud to be recognised as the #1 WORK180 Endorsed Employer in the Top 101 Employers for Women 2026. Learn more.



- Career development: At EY, your career is yours to shape! We’ll develop you with future-focused skills and equip you with world-class experiences com/au/careerdevelopment
- Flexible work arrangements: Our flexible work policies empower you to balance your professional and personal life, fostering a culture of trust and autonomy.
- A comprehensive benefits package: From a yearly wellness incentive, to access to additional 8 weeks of flex leave per year, and family-friendly policies, including 26 weeks of gender-neutral paid parental leave, we cater to your diverse needs to help you thrive both personally and professionally www.ey.com/au/benefits 
- Salary: We offer a competitive salary which is open to negotiation pending on skills and experience.

Acknowledgement of Country

EY acknowledges the Traditional Owners and Custodians of the lands on which EY offices are located around Australia. We pay our respects to their cultures, and to their Elders — past, present, and emerging. Find out more about our vision for reconciliation at ey.com/en_au/careers/indigenous

Inclusiveness is core to who we are and how we work together, driving value for our people and for our business. We encourage applications from people of all ages, nationalities, abilities, cultures, sexual orientations, and gender identities and are committed to providing an equitable and barrier free recruitment experience for all. We encourage you to share any support and adjustments you need to be your best and participate equitably in our recruitment process. We understand sharing your needs with us can be daunting, so if you have questions before or during your application, we welcome you to get in touch at contactrecruitment@au.ey.com or +61 3 8650 7788 (option 2). Anything you tell us will be kept completely confidential.

Are you ready to shape your future with confidence? Apply today.

opportunity.job_description:
About the Job


Supervisor / Manager in a growing industry specialised firm (Brisbane based)
 
Newpoint Advisory (NA) provides financial analysis, restructuring and turnaround, and formal insolvency services to the property and construction industries across Australia. Our assignments range from distressed development and builder IAs to Builder Financial Reviews and Insolvency matters across property and builder restructures, property management and completion of distressed property developments.
 
NA’s core strategy is to help stakeholders mitigate risk and make informed credit and recovery decisions and is a trusted advisor to its clients, comprising secured lenders, developers and builders. For more information see NA’s website: www.newpointadvisory.com


This role suits a candidate with accounting / insolvency experience, who has a keen interest in the property and construction industries.
 
Qualifications and Experience Required:

- +4 years of insolvency and advisory experience including management of staff.
- Property and construction experience preferred, but not essential.
- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or Economics.
- CA/CPA qualified and willing to complete ARITA course (if not completed).
- Clear written and verbal communications skills.
- Commercial attitude to problem solving, negotiation and timely decisions.
- Motivated and efficient with an ability to take ownership of assigned matters and coordinate multiple work streams.
 
Tasks and Responsibilities:

- Part of the senior management team for business management and growth strategy.
- Workflow will generally include:
- Detailed financial modelling, forecast cashflow and feasibility analysis.
- Identify, analyse and implement strategic and creative options to maximise property realisations and outcomes across a range of distressed property types and locations.
- Coordinate lawyers, sales agents, builders, and other consultants to deliver target outcomes.
- Prepare reports for and engage with clients and creditors.
- Oversee statutory insolvency processes and procedures to mitigate risks.
- Staff management: mentor and develop staff and ensure achievement of required deadlines and quality expectations across multiple workstreams.
- Marketing: identify, formulate and support marketing efforts for existing clients and to secure new clients.
 
Why join NA:

- Growing team with collaborative working environment that encourages development of skills, service lines and clients.
- Flat structure with high autonomy and access to diverse industry client base.
- Training support and mentoring from a diversified team of professionals (finance, property, construction and insolvency).
- Option to work remotely.
- Access to high profile distressed property/construction projects across Eastern seaboard.
- Exposure to high-profile matters.
- Above market salary plus bonus potential.

opportunity.job_description:
Forensic Accountant – Assistant Manager / Senior Consultant
Leading Advisory Firm | Melbourne CBD


Join a leading specialist advisory firm working on complex, high-value matters where your analysis directly impacts real commercial outcomes.
This is an excellent opportunity for an Auditor looking to transition into forensic accounting, or an existing forensic accounting professional seeking broader exposure to valuations and disputes work. Full training and mentoring will be provided.


In this role, you’ll build on your audit and financial analysis experience by:

- Conducting detailed financial investigations, damages assessments and business valuations.
- Analysing complex accounting issues and applying your knowledge of financial reporting in a disputes and litigation context.
- Building advanced financial models in Excel, including discounted cash flow (DCF) analyses.
- Contributing to clear, well-structured expert reports that assist courts and parties in understanding the financial issues in a case.
- Working closely with leading litigation lawyers and recognised expert witnesses on high-profile matters.
- Developing strong professional relationships and laying the groundwork to become an expert witness in the future.


Why this will appeal

- Clear pathway from Audit into Forensic Accounting
- Strong exposure to valuations and financial modelling
- Work on complex, high-value matters across disputes and investigations
- Direct mentoring from experienced forensic specialists
- Supportive, high-performing team within a global firm


Who they’re looking for

- 2–4 years’ experience in External Audit or Forensic Accounting
- CA qualified (or near completion)
- Strong Excel skills with exposure to financial modelling
- Interest in valuations, investigations or disputes work
- Strong communication and report-writing skills


Salary: circa $125,000 package
Eligibility: Full Australian working rights required.


Keen to know more?
Contact Helen Cramp at Troy Recruitment on 0413 198 073 or helen@troyrecruitment.com,
or connect on LinkedIn.
